proposal.diagnosis: The baseline remains upright for 20 seconds but has no touchdowns and identical results at both commands: target_vx currently has no policy connection. Add symmetric command-dependent ankle drive opposing the existing positive forward-velocity feedback. At 0.50 m/s this subtracts 0.45 normalized action before clipping; at zero command the standing policy is exactly unchanged. This experiment tests forward propulsion and its stability limits, not yet an alternating gait.

plan.hypothesis: Negative ankle command coupling will produce a forward weight shift and positive velocity while existing feedback limits acceleration. Symmetric double support may constrain travel, revealing whether explicit unloading is needed next.
plan.readout: Measure command-aligned velocity and displacement, pitch, pelvis height, ankle clipping, foot loads and contact edges. Positive velocity with bounded pitch supports the drive sign; backward motion opposes it. Persistent double support despite forward lean indicates a stepping limitation. Distinguish foot sliding and incidental edges from alternating footfalls. Compare zero-command standing and recovery after command removal.

proposal.diagnosis: r01 produces forward weight shift, not sustained propulsion: seed 273 slows from 0.113 m/s to 0.002 m/s while both feet remain planted, then develops lateral instability and falls. Increasing ankle drive alone is therefore unsupported. Retain r01 and add command-dependent left-leg shortening: at 0.50 m/s, knee and hip targets change by approximately +0.289 and -0.142 rad. This tests deliberate unloading and forward placement before attempting alternation. Zero-command coefficients remain unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Coordinated left knee flexion and hip flexion can release the planted left foot under the existing forward drive, rather than merely moving the pelvis over stationary feet. Failure to maintain right support would identify lateral transfer as the immediate limitation.
plan.readout: Measure left load reduction, clearance above its initial ankle height, forward foot displacement, right support load, pelvis height, roll and lateral velocity around lift-off. An early left_off with clearance and bounded torso attitude supports deliberate unloading; contact chatter, continued double support, or lift-off only during collapse opposes it. After command removal, inspect touchdown placement and standing recovery. A single contact edge is not evidence of walking.

proposal.diagnosis: r02 briefly unloads the left foot, but it replants within 0.06–0.08 seconds. The pelvis then accelerates leftward, roll becomes negative, and positive hip-roll targets saturate; the right foot lifts during collapse. The recorded right touchdown occurs after uprightness is lost, not during successful walking. Retain the r02 sagittal edits and add a common negative hip-roll command offset to test rightward support transfer. At 0.50 m/s this changes both native roll targets by -0.172 rad; zero-command behavior remains unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Rightward lateral positioning can counter the leftward collapse induced by left-leg shortening, allowing the right foot to remain supportive while the left foot clears. A constant offset may still be insufficient without state-dependent transfer.
plan.readout: Compare the first 0.5 and 1.5 seconds after command onset with r02: lateral velocity, roll, hip-roll clipping, right load, left clearance and air duration. Favor bounded roll and sustained right support with genuine left clearance. Oppose persistent leftward collapse, a reversed rightward fall, or both feet remaining planted. Inspect touchdown and recovery after command removal; do not count post-collapse touchdowns as progress.

proposal.diagnosis: r03 contradicts the assumed lateral transfer sign. At 0.10 seconds, seed 273 has lateral velocity +0.260 m/s versus +0.074 in r02; upright duration drops from 1.24 to 0.96 seconds. Negative hip-roll offsets initially increase positive roll but accelerate the pelvis leftward, worsening support loss. Reverse only these two command coefficients, retaining all r03 sagittal terms. The new offset is +0.172 rad at 0.50 m/s and remains zero when standing.

plan.hypothesis: Positive common hip-roll command offsets will shift the pelvis toward right support and oppose the leftward motion caused by left-leg shortening. This may improve left clearance, although constant offsets cannot themselves generate alternation.
plan.readout: Compare early lateral velocity, pelvis displacement, roll, right-foot load and left clearance against r02/r03, especially at 0.10, 0.24 and 0.50 seconds after command onset. Reduced leftward velocity with maintained right support favors the reversed sign. Rightward collapse, excessive roll, or no sustained clearance opposes this magnitude or the simultaneous-transfer strategy. Measure upright duration and recovery separately from contact-edge counts.

proposal.diagnosis: r04 initially moves rightward as intended, but persistent left-leg shortening still produces negative roll, hip-roll saturation and leftward collapse. Seed 273's right touchdown at 1.44 seconds precedes uprightness loss by only 0.12 seconds and does not establish stable stepping. Replace the constant left-leg shortening with roll-sensitive hidden-unit feedback, retaining the other r04 terms. At command 0.50 and roll zero, the added knee action remains approximately 0.250; at roll -0.30 it falls to 0.054, allowing the leg to extend before severe collapse. At zero command the two hidden contributions cancel exactly.

plan.hypothesis: Reducing left-leg shortening as negative roll develops will interrupt the collapse mechanism and permit supportive replanting without eliminating the initial unloading impulse.
plan.readout: Inspect knee and hip targets as roll crosses -0.10 and -0.30 rad, then actual leg extension, pelvis height, lateral velocity, support loads and hip-roll saturation. Earlier supportive replanting with bounded roll favors the hypothesis. Continued collapse despite target extension indicates insufficient authority or a different mechanism; stable double support without clearance indicates excessive suppression. Count only upright, advancing footfalls as locomotion progress.

proposal.diagnosis: r05 prevents collapse in all three trials, but settles into double support with no qualified touchdowns. Seed 273 remains upright for 20 seconds yet advances only 0.235 m; persistent negative roll and left hip-roll limit contact indicate a one-sided equilibrium. Retain the successful left-leg feedback, add its right-side mirror, and replace the constant lateral offset with the difference between left and right flexion signals. This tests reciprocal support exchange rather than increasing propulsion. All added contributions cancel exactly at zero command.

plan.hypothesis: Mirrored roll-sensitive leg shortening and differential lateral positioning can turn one-sided unloading into reciprocal load transfer. The principal competing outcome is symmetric crouching or damped rocking without foot clearance.
plan.readout: Measure left/right knee-target difference, roll, lateral velocity, alternating load minima, foot clearance, air duration and forward touchdown placement. Repeated upright load exchanges with advancing alternating footfalls favor the hypothesis. Simultaneous knee flexion with reduced pelvis height, static double support, or growing lateral oscillation oppose it. Report sustained forward speed separately from initial displacement and verify standing recovery.

proposal.diagnosis: r06 exposes an algebraic defect: at command 0.50, tanh(1+6r)-tanh(-1+6r) is even in roll r. Thus the mirrored flexion signals are identical, and their lateral difference vanishes. The measured simultaneous unloading, symmetric crouch and absent alternation match this defect. Shift all four hidden biases to -2.0, retaining every output coefficient. At roll zero, added knee action decreases from 0.250 to 0.158; at roll +0.15, left/right additions become approximately 0.249/0.046, reversing for negative roll. Zero-command cancellation remains exact.

plan.hypothesis: Removing the accidental even symmetry will produce genuinely reciprocal leg shortening and lateral positioning, rather than bilateral crouching. Whether this yields sustained stepping or merely damped load transfer remains untested.
plan.readout: Verify unequal knee targets at nonzero roll and reversal of that difference when roll changes sign. Measure pelvis height, alternating foot loads, clearance, air duration, advancing touchdowns, roll amplitude and hip-roll clipping. Repeated upright alternating footfalls favor the hypothesis; symmetric crouching, static asymmetric support, or growing lateral collapse oppose it. Separate transient forward displacement from sustained velocity and assess recovery at zero command.

proposal.diagnosis: r07 generates reciprocal rocking, but not foot release: seed 273 repeatedly raises an ankle origin to roughly 0.09–0.10 m while that foot still bears substantial load. Its ankle targets remain positive during these attempted lifts, suggesting the standing ankle drive may maintain toe contact. Add negative ankle offsets coupled to each existing flexion signal, retaining all r07 terms. At command 0.50 and roll zero the offset is approximately -0.578 normalized action; it becomes stronger on the selected flexing side. Zero-command contributions cancel exactly. Toe-contact interference is a hypothesis, not established by ankle height alone.

plan.hypothesis: Coordinating ankle withdrawal with hip and knee flexion will release residual foot contact and convert reciprocal rocking into actual swing intervals, without increasing knee shortening.
plan.readout: Compare flexing-side ankle targets and angles, contact loads, clearance, air duration and forward foot placement against r07. Sustained unloading followed by upright advancing touchdowns supports ankle interference. Continued loaded contact despite ankle motion, simultaneous loss of both supports, backward motion or earlier collapse opposes this revision. Track alternating runs and sustained forward speed separately; verify recovery after command removal.

proposal.diagnosis: r08 adds substantial bilateral forward drive rather than achieving foot release. Seed 273 reaches 1.836 m/s with both feet trailing approximately 0.71 m at collapse; no qualified touchdowns occur. Replace the ankle additions with their antisymmetric component: left receives -0.3 times the left-minus-right flexion signal, and right receives the opposite. This removes the added common-mode ankle drive while preserving r08's left-right ankle-action difference before clipping. All other r08 coefficients remain unchanged, and zero-command cancellation is preserved.

plan.hypothesis: Differential ankle coordination can assist reciprocal unloading without the common-mode acceleration that caused r08's forward collapse. If loaded contact persists, ankle coordination alone is insufficient.
plan.readout: Compare forward acceleration, trailing-foot distance, ankle clipping and upright duration with r08. Verify that added ankle actions sum to zero before clipping, then inspect alternating load reductions, actual clearance, air duration and advancing touchdowns. Bounded forward motion with genuine reciprocal release favors the hypothesis; renewed forward collapse or loaded rocking without steps opposes it. Evaluate zero-command recovery separately.

proposal.diagnosis: r09 delays but does not prevent forward collapse: all trials lack qualified touchdowns, and seed 273 reaches 1.817 m/s with both feet approximately 0.69 m behind the pelvis. Reciprocal rocking has not produced forward replacement of support. Increase differential hip-pitch coupling while preserving its common-mode component: the more-flexed leg receives stronger forward hip flexion and the opposite leg receives relative extension. For a left-minus-right hidden flexion signal of 1.0, this adds approximately -0.191/+0.191 rad to the respective hip targets. Retain all r09 ankle, knee and lateral terms; zero-command behavior remains unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Insufficient fore-aft leg separation is preventing the rocking motion from becoming advancing footfalls. Stronger differential hip motion may bring the unloading foot forward before the pelvis outruns its support.
plan.readout: Measure hip-target separation, actual hip angles, each foot's forward displacement during unloading, clearance, loads and touchdown position relative to the pelvis. Upright advancing touchdowns followed by opposite-side release favor the hypothesis. Loaded-foot sliding, larger shear without clearance, or unchanged trailing-foot collapse oppose it. Track pelvis height, pitch, ankle saturation and sustained speed; distinguish reduced acceleration from genuine stepping.

proposal.diagnosis: r10 produces genuine advancing touchdowns before collapse, unlike r09, but placement overshoots: seed 273's left foot reaches 0.501 m ahead of the pelvis, followed by backward motion, bilateral negative ankle saturation and height loss. Its recorded alternation occurs after the upright prefix ends. Reduce differential hip gain from 0.1672 to 0.1000 while preserving the common-mode gain and every other r10 coefficient. This brackets the transition between r09's ineffective placement and r10's excessive reach. Zero-command cancellation remains exact.

plan.hypothesis: Moderate differential hip motion will retain foot release while shortening placement enough to accept weight and initiate the opposite step. Shared foot-position feedback may still destabilize landing even with shorter reach.
plan.readout: Measure each advancing touchdown's foot-relative X, clearance, air duration, impact load, pelvis velocity and height. Favor shorter forward placement followed by sustained support and an opposite-side upright touchdown. No clearance indicates insufficient amplitude; repeated same-side steps, bilateral ankle saturation, backward velocity or height collapse after landing oppose the hypothesis. Compare upright alternating runs rather than total contact counts.

proposal.diagnosis: r11 achieves one early advancing touchdown in seed 273, but both ankle actions subsequently saturate negative as the advanced foot moves farther ahead; backward motion and height collapse follow. Both ankles currently respond equally to either foot's X position, so swing placement directly perturbs the opposite support ankle. Replace this shared position feedback with ipsilateral feedback, preserving its value when both feet have equal X offsets. Retain every other r11 coefficient. Unlike previous command-canceling edits, this can change asymmetric standing and requires an explicit standing trial.

plan.hypothesis: Decoupling ankle position feedback will prevent an advancing foot from dragging the support ankle into the same saturation, allowing weight acceptance and opposite-side release. Doubling local sensitivity could instead destabilize individual feet.
plan.readout: Inspect opposite-ankle action during each foot's forward excursion, bilateral saturation duration, support load, touchdown placement, pelvis height and velocity. Favor advancing touchdowns followed by stable support and upright alternation. Oppose stronger local clipping, foot sliding, backward collapse or degraded zero-command balance. Compare standing drift and upright duration with the original standing results.

proposal.diagnosis: r12 preserves 20-second standing in seed 271 and separates ankle responses during placement: at seed 273's touchdown, left/right ankle actions are -1.0/+0.551. Nevertheless, backward collapse persists. Both hips still flex in response to either foot advancing: their shared -0.2 foot-X terms reinforce flexion as the pelvis retreats behind the feet. Remove only these four coefficients to test this potential feedback loop, retaining r12's local ankle feedback and differential stepping terms. Standing is not mathematically unchanged and must be retested.

plan.hypothesis: Removing shared foot-position-driven hip flexion will prevent one advancing foot from pulling both legs forward during weight acceptance, improving height retention and permitting opposite-side stepping.
plan.readout: After the first advancing touchdown, compare common hip targets, actual hip angles, pelvis height, forward velocity, foot-relative X and ankle saturation with r12. Stable weight acceptance followed by an upright opposite-side touchdown favors the hypothesis. Continued backward collapse despite reduced common hip flexion implicates ankle feedback or support geometry instead. Also inspect pitch stability and displacement throughout the standing trial.

proposal.diagnosis: Removing shared hip-position feedback did not prevent backward collapse. In seed 273, yaw grows from -0.231 rad at touchdown to -0.557 at 3.0 seconds and -1.211 at height loss, while lateral velocity also grows. This rotation compromises world-X foot placement and may contribute to support failure. Retain r13 and add bilateral hip-yaw angle/rate feedback, testing whether stance reaction torque can restrain heading drift. The proposed sign assumes positive hip-yaw targets generate negative pelvis-yaw reaction under support; this requires measurement.

plan.hypothesis: Hip-yaw feedback will reduce heading rotation during asymmetric foot loading, improving placement and weight acceptance. If yaw is merely a consequence of failed sagittal support, heading control alone will not prevent collapse.
plan.readout: Check the sign of yaw acceleration following yaw-target changes, yaw rate and angle around first unloading and touchdown, hip-yaw clipping, lateral velocity, pelvis height and forward velocity. Reduced yaw growth with longer upright support and opposite-side stepping favors the hypothesis. Amplified yaw rejects the sign; bounded yaw with unchanged backward collapse rejects heading drift as the principal limitation. Verify standing because these terms remain active at zero command.

proposal.diagnosis: r14 reduces heading rotation but barely changes upright duration: seed 273 lasts 3.74 seconds versus 3.72 in r13. Its alternating touchdown occurs during backward descent, not sustained walking. The advanced ankle remains negatively saturated, followed by bilateral saturation as backward velocity grows. Halve ipsilateral foot-X sensitivity from -12 to -6 while retaining yaw control, velocity feedback and all other r14 terms. This tests excessive ankle position correction without restoring cross-foot coupling. Standing equilibrium may change.

plan.hypothesis: Lower ankle position sensitivity will reduce saturation after forward placement and allow the pelvis to progress over the new support rather than retreat. Remaining velocity feedback may still dominate saturation or reduced position stiffness may destabilize standing.
plan.readout: Compare ankle preclip contributions and clipping duration around touchdown, actual ankle angles, support loads, pelvis velocity and height. Favor reduced negative saturation followed by forward weight acceptance and upright alternating steps. Unchanged clipping dominated by qvel_0, persistent backward collapse, or new forward runaway opposes the hypothesis. Measure standing displacement, pitch and height over the full horizon.

proposal.diagnosis: r15's reduced position gain destroys standing: seed 271 falls backward after only 2.12 upright seconds. Walking also remains unstable, so reduced position sensitivity is unsupported. Undo those two coefficients individually and reduce ankle velocity gain from 4.5 to 3.5, retaining all other r15 terms. This tests whether strong velocity feedback aggravates post-placement saturation while restoring the position sensitivity previously compatible with standing; it does not restore an earlier checkpoint.

plan.hypothesis: Restored ankle position sensitivity with moderately reduced velocity sensitivity will retain standing stability while reducing saturation during backward motion after touchdown. Reduced damping could instead increase oscillation or forward runaway.
plan.readout: First assess full-horizon standing, pitch, displacement and ankle clipping. During walking, separate position and velocity contributions to ankle saturation around touchdown; measure backward acceleration, pelvis height, support loads and upright alternating footfalls. Favor preserved standing plus improved weight acceptance. Standing failure, stronger oscillation, forward runaway or unchanged post-touchdown collapse opposes the revision.

proposal.diagnosis: r16 restores 20-second standing, but walking still lacks reliable support replacement: seed 273 remains in contact until forward collapse, while seed 272 produces only one qualified touchdown. Retain r16's ankle gains and increase differential knee shortening, pairing swing-side flexion with opposite-side extension. The common knee contribution is unchanged, while the left-right gain rises from 0.164 to 0.324. For a hidden flexion-signal difference of 1.0, native knee targets change by +0.0924/-0.0924 rad. Zero-command behavior remains exactly unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Greater leg-length contrast will create actual swing clearance while the opposite leg supports pelvis height, allowing existing hip placement to produce alternating steps rather than loaded rocking.
plan.readout: Measure selected-side load reduction, clearance and air duration, opposite knee extension and support load, pelvis height, touchdown advance and subsequent side exchange. Favor repeated advancing upright footfalls without bilateral unloading. Increased crouching, support-knee collapse, simultaneous flight, or unchanged planted-foot forward runaway opposes the hypothesis. Check recovery after command removal and distinguish transient motion from sustained 0.50 m/s tracking.

proposal.diagnosis: r17 increases unloading but does not organize alternation: seed 272 makes three qualified left touchdowns without a right touchdown, then collapses backward. Roll-only selection can repeatedly advance the same foot. Add fore-aft foot separation to the existing hidden pairs so an advancing foot suppresses its own flexion signal and favors the trailing leg. A 0.20 m left lead shifts the left/right hidden arguments by -0.8/+0.8. Retain every r17 output coefficient. Matching additions within each hidden pair preserve exact zero-command cancellation.

plan.hypothesis: Foot-separation feedback will terminate repeated same-side advancement and transfer flexion toward the trailing leg, producing shorter placements and reciprocal support exchange.
plan.readout: Track hidden flexion-signal differences against foot separation and roll, especially immediately after advancing touchdowns. Favor suppression of the leading leg's flexion followed by trailing-leg clearance and an upright opposite-side touchdown. Repeated same-side stepping, stalled split stance, rapid switching without clearance, or backward height collapse oppose the hypothesis. Measure sustained forward speed and zero-command recovery separately from contact-edge counts.

proposal.diagnosis: r18 produces short alternating sequences in seeds 272 and 273, but their feet advance while the pelvis retreats and loses height; seed 271 instead overruns planted feet. Placement currently lacks direct forward-velocity feedback. Add symmetric hip-pitch velocity coupling: positive velocity increases forward flexion, while backward velocity retracts the legs. At +/-0.50 m/s this changes native hip targets by -/+0.255 rad. Retain every r18 coefficient. This also affects standing transients, requiring regression testing.

plan.hypothesis: Velocity-sensitive hip placement will reduce both excessive forward reach during backward motion and insufficient reach during forward motion, allowing the emerging alternation to retain support beneath the moving pelvis.
plan.readout: Measure hip-target changes versus velocity, touchdown X relative to the pelvis, subsequent velocity and height, ankle clipping, and upright alternating runs. Favor reduced backward acceleration after landing and smaller trailing-foot excursions during forward motion. Increased stance-leg shear, oscillation, loss of clearance or unchanged collapse opposes the hypothesis. Verify full-horizon zero-command balance and command-removal recovery.

proposal.diagnosis: r19 retains standing but does not improve weight acceptance or alternation. Advancing feet again approach the negative ankle limit before backward collapse. The ankle self-angle coefficient 1.43885 nearly cancels the native position servo's restoring stiffness because the action half-range is 0.695 rad. Reduce that coefficient to 1.0 and compensate each bias so its contribution is unchanged at ankle angle -0.40 rad. This adds restoring stiffness around that posture while retaining all r19 placement and balance feedback; standing still needs verification.

plan.hypothesis: Restoring some ankle posture stiffness will limit extreme ankle excursions during placement and improve load acceptance, rather than allowing the feedback-driven target to follow the joint toward its limit.
plan.readout: Measure ankle target-minus-angle error, actual ankle excursions, hard-limit proximity, clipping duration and contact loads around touchdown. Favor reduced extreme dorsiflexion with retained clearance, pelvis height and upright opposite-side stepping. Persistent saturation that masks the stiffness change, lost clearance, increased impacts or standing instability opposes the revision. Report forward velocity and upright alternating runs separately from incidental contact edges.

proposal.diagnosis: r20 preserves standing but leaves walking failure essentially unchanged: seed 273 again loses uprightness at 2.40 seconds, with declining pelvis height and saturated ankles. Add common knee height feedback while retaining all r20 terms. The added action is 1.5*(pelvis_height-0.98), zero at reset height; at 0.90 m it extends each knee target by approximately 0.139 rad. This tests support-height loss directly rather than further adjusting ankle feedback. It may also suppress needed swing clearance.

plan.hypothesis: Height-dependent knee extension will improve weight acceptance and interrupt progressive sinking during the emerging foot exchanges, without eliminating differential leg shortening.
plan.readout: Measure pelvis height and vertical velocity before and after touchdown, knee targets and angles, support loads, swing clearance and upright alternating runs. Favor arrested height loss with continued opposite-side release and forward progression. Loss of clearance, impact spikes, bouncing, or continued collapse despite knee extension opposes the hypothesis. Verify standing because height feedback remains active at zero command.

proposal.diagnosis: r21 improves standing height slightly but does not arrest walking collapse. Foot separation also grows substantially: seed 273 widens from approximately 0.41 m at reset to 0.69 m by 1.98 seconds, before severe height loss. Add differential hip-roll feedback around 0.40 m lateral separation, retaining every other r21 term. The added left/right actions are -/+0.5*(separation-0.40), preserving their mean. At 0.70 m separation this applies approximately -/+0.0645 rad of corrective hip-roll target.

plan.hypothesis: Restraining progressive stance widening will improve support geometry and preserve leg extension capacity during foot exchanges. Excessive correction could instead cause foot crossing or reduce lateral balance authority.
plan.readout: Track lateral foot separation, individual foot motion, hip-roll angles and clipping, pelvis height, lateral velocity and support loads. Favor bounded separation with retained clearance, longer upright alternating runs and forward progression. Foot crossing, increased sliding, reduced unloading or unchanged collapse despite controlled width opposes the hypothesis. Verify standing drift and command-removal recovery because this feedback remains active at zero command.

proposal.diagnosis: r22 restrains standing-width drift but does not improve walking survival. Walking still exhibits rapid unloading/reloading, short air intervals and large load transfers before collapse. The hidden leg-selection signals use roll angle but not roll rate, potentially reacting too late to lateral reversal. Add mirrored roll-rate terms equivalent to approximately 0.10 seconds of roll prediction near upright. Retain all r22 coefficients; matching terms within each hidden pair preserve exact zero-command cancellation.

plan.hypothesis: Anticipatory roll feedback will improve the timing of leg shortening and lateral transfer, reducing abrupt reloads and allowing longer, better-supported swing intervals. Excessive anticipation may instead suppress stepping or accelerate switching.
plan.readout: Compare roll-rate peaks, hidden-signal reversals relative to contact edges, air durations, peak foot loads and pelvis vertical velocity. Favor smoother support exchange with retained forward clearance and longer upright alternating runs. Damped double support without steps, faster contact chatter, larger impacts or unchanged backward collapse opposes the hypothesis. Compare direct command onset with a ramp and inspect zero-command recovery.

proposal.diagnosis: r23 makes all three trials upright for 20 seconds and permits command-removal recovery, but suppresses sustained unloading entirely. Seed 273 settles near zero velocity after only 0.153 m displacement. Together with r22's unstable foot exchanges, this identifies roll-rate coupling as a strong damping lever. Halve its magnitude to 0.3, equivalent to approximately 0.05 seconds of roll prediction, while retaining every other r23 term. Zero-command behavior remains unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Intermediate roll-rate feedback may retain enough damping to prevent destructive load transfers while permitting a bounded stepping oscillation. The alternative is continued static double support or renewed divergent rocking.
plan.readout: Measure growth or decay of roll oscillations, roll-rate peaks, alternating load minima, clearance, air duration and upright advancing touchdowns. Favor repeated bounded support exchanges with sustained forward velocity and successful stopping. Static settling indicates excessive damping; increasing oscillation amplitude, impacts or height loss indicates insufficient damping. Do not treat longer survival alone as walking progress.

proposal.diagnosis: r24 remains upright and recovers after stopping, but halving roll-rate coupling from 0.6 to 0.3 produces essentially the same stationary double-support equilibrium. Earlier zero-rate coupling produced unstable foot exchanges. Test a smaller nonzero magnitude of 0.1 to locate whether bounded unloading exists between these regimes. Retain all other r24 coefficients; zero-command behavior remains exactly unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: A roll-rate coefficient of 0.1 may permit sustained reciprocal unloading while retaining enough anticipation to limit the divergent rocking observed without it. A useful intermediate regime is not yet established.
plan.readout: Compare early and late roll-amplitude envelopes, load minima, clearance, air duration and upright advancing touchdown sequences. Favor bounded repeated alternation with forward progression. Decay to double support indicates continued suppression; growing oscillations, repeated same-side impacts or height collapse indicate insufficient damping. Compare ramped and direct command onset and measure stopping recovery.

proposal.diagnosis: r25 preserved upright survival and stopping recovery, but produced no qualified steps. Unlike r24, late load oscillations became appreciable without sustained forward motion. This suggests proximity to an unloading threshold, not demonstrated walking.

plan.hypothesis: Reducing hidden roll-rate coupling from ±0.10 to ±0.06 will permit actual reciprocal foot release while retaining some protection against the divergent exchanges observed at zero coupling. All other r25 coefficients remain unchanged; paired hidden contributions still cancel at zero command.
plan.readout: Compare early and late roll-amplitude envelopes, alternating minimum foot loads, clearance and air duration against r25. Require advancing touchdowns followed by supported opposite-side steps, maintained pelvis height and sustained forward speed. Growing oscillations followed by backward collapse reject useful stabilization; continued double support indicates the release threshold remains unmet. Check recovery after command removal rather than counting survival alone.

proposal.diagnosis: r26 produced substantial reciprocal loading but no qualified steps in the two surviving trials; the ramped trial eventually collapsed backward. Further reducing damping risks amplifying rocking without solving clearance. Test leg-length contrast while retaining r26 timing.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing differential knee modulation while preserving its common component will convert partial unloading into swing clearance, with opposite-leg extension retaining support. Keeping hidden roll-rate coupling at ±0.06 may limit the instability previously seen with stronger knee contrast. Zero-command hidden contributions remain cancelled; all unlisted r26 weights stay unchanged.
plan.readout: Measure minimum swing-side load, actual knee-angle contrast, foot clearance and air duration, opposite-side support load, and pelvis vertical velocity. Favor repeated upright advancing alternation with sustained forward progression. Larger load oscillations without release, simultaneous unloading, impact spikes or renewed backward collapse reject the hypothesis. Compare ramped versus direct onset and assess stopping recovery.

proposal.diagnosis: r27 increased same-side stepping in the ramped trial but accelerated backward collapse. The other trials remained upright without qualified steps. Knee contrast alone did not solve support exchange; advancing-foot ankle saturation remains a candidate limitation.

plan.hypothesis: Halving differential ankle foot-position sensitivity while preserving common-position sensitivity will reduce extreme opposing ankle commands during foot separation, improving landing acceptance without repeating r15's loss of common standing stiffness. Retain all other r27 coefficients, including knee contrast and roll-rate coupling.
plan.readout: Separate common and differential foot-position contributions to ankle commands. Around foot advancement, measure clipping duration, ankle angles, touchdown placement, support loads, pelvis velocity and height. Favor clearance followed by forward weight acceptance and upright opposite-side stepping. Bilateral clipping, backward collapse, loss of release or standing drift reject the hypothesis. Surviving planted rocking is not walking success.

proposal.diagnosis: r28 preserved standing and delayed the ramped trial's collapse, but its sole alternation occurred during severe height loss. Direct onset still produced loaded rocking with both feet behind the pelvis and no qualified steps. Test coordinated hip excursion rather than further increasing knee shortening.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing differential hip-pitch modulation by 50%, while preserving its common component, will move the shortening leg forward sufficiently to complete a swing. Retain r28 ankle feedback and roll-rate coupling. Excessive reach may instead reproduce backward landing failure; all unlisted coefficients remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Measure hip-angle contrast, swing-foot forward velocity, clearance, air duration and touchdown X relative to the pelvis. Favor forward placement followed by sustained support and upright opposite-side release, with increasing sustained speed toward 0.50 m/s. Longer reach followed by negative ankle saturation, backward acceleration or height loss rejects the hypothesis. Distinguish stepping from sliding and verify standing and stopping recovery.

proposal.diagnosis: r29 enabled earlier alternation in the ramped trial, but the pelvis barely advanced while feet landed increasingly ahead, followed by bilateral ankle saturation and backward collapse. Direct onset still settled into loaded rocking. Increased hip excursion did not establish forward weight transfer.

plan.hypothesis: Stronger command-dependent ankle drive will increase forward pelvis progression before touchdown, improving alignment between body motion and the existing swing excursion. This cannot correct an already clipped ankle command and may instead cause planted-foot forward runaway. Change only these two r29 coefficients; zero-command outputs are unchanged.
plan.readout: Measure pelvis velocity immediately before foot release and touchdown, touchdown X relative to the pelvis, ankle clipping onset, and subsequent support loads and height. Favor forward progression through successive upright alternating landings, not larger initial displacement. Persistent backward collapse, earlier clipping, or forward acceleration without foot release rejects the hypothesis. Measure sustained speed against 0.50 m/s and recovery after stopping.

proposal.diagnosis: r30 improved initial weight acceptance in the ramped trial: two alternating qualified landings occurred with pelvis height near 0.96 m and forward velocity reaching 0.203 m/s. However, stepping stopped; direct-onset trials never established qualified steps and eventually overran planted feet at approximately 2 m/s. More propulsion is therefore unsupported. From r30, increase only mirrored hidden roll sensitivity from 6 to 9 to test whether stronger state-dependent leg selection can renew unloading before support falls behind. Retain ankle drive, placement feedback and roll-rate coefficients. Matched hidden pairs still cancel exactly at zero command.

plan.hypothesis: Greater roll sensitivity will amplify differential leg shortening and lateral transfer during small load oscillations, producing earlier reciprocal release under the existing forward drive. It may instead amplify destructive rocking or premature switching.
plan.readout: Compare roll, knee-target contrast, support loads, clearance and air duration before release against r30. Favor repeated qualified alternating touchdowns while height remains stable, feet replace trailing support, and sustained velocity approaches 0.50 m/s. Reject growing roll oscillations, contact chatter without clearance, backward landing collapse, or renewed planted-foot forward runaway. Record ankle clipping, touchdown-relative X and post-touchdown velocity. In the short pulse trial, assess standing recovery rather than interpreting survival alone as walking.

proposal.diagnosis: r31 enables repeated release: seed 273 sustains approximately 0.19–0.20 m/s temporarily, but both feet progressively move ahead of the pelvis, bilateral negative ankle clipping develops, and backward collapse follows. The ramped trial similarly overreaches. Retain r31's roll sensitivity and remove only the common-mode hidden hip-flexion contribution, preserving differential hip gain at 0.15. Near symmetric activation at 0.50 m/s, this extends both hip targets by approximately 0.090 rad. This tests excessive common forward placement without weakening differential swing excursion. Zero-command outputs remain exactly unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Removing shared command-dependent hip flexion will keep average foot placement closer to the moving pelvis, delaying negative ankle saturation and allowing reciprocal unloading to continue without backward collapse.
plan.readout: Compare mean foot-relative X, hip angles, pelvis velocity and ankle clipping against r31, especially during seed 273's first three seconds. Favor bounded average foot placement, preserved clearance, qualified alternating landings and sustained upright forward speed approaching 0.50 m/s. Loss of release, feet remaining behind during forward runaway, or continued backward collapse despite reduced forward placement opposes the hypothesis. Check support loads, height and recovery after command removal; contact chatter or sliding alone is not success.

proposal.diagnosis: r32 extended seed 273's upright duration from 3.88 to 8.36 seconds and maintained approximately 0.20 m/s through several seconds of foot exchanges. Nevertheless, negative ankle clipping and backward collapse returned; ramped onset and stopping did not improve materially. Test a smaller further common hip-extension increment while retaining r32's differential gain of 0.15 and every other coefficient. The added action is 0.01*((h0-h1)+(h2-h3)) on each hip, approximately +0.055 rad near symmetric activation at 0.50 m/s. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: A modest additional common hip extension will reduce residual forward placement bias and prolong supported progression without removing the differential swing motion. Excessive extension could instead leave support behind the pelvis.
plan.readout: Compare seed 273's velocity, mean foot-relative X, pitch, height and ankle-clipping duration through seconds 2–8 against r32. Favor sustained qualified alternating footfalls with bounded placement and speed progressing toward 0.50 m/s, not merely longer survival. Forward runaway, lost clearance, increasingly negative pitch or unchanged backward collapse rejects the increment. Separately assess ramped-onset robustness and recovery from the identical short command pulse.

proposal.diagnosis: r33 achieves 20-second upright progression in seed 273, but at only 0.202 m/s with sparse qualified alternation. The ramped trial still repeatedly advances the leading left foot: near 7 seconds, roll is +0.12 rad and left lead is 0.146 m, so the selector still favors left flexion (9*0.12-4*0.146≈0.50, excluding rate). Double foot-separation feedback to make that contribution approximately -0.09 instead, favoring the trailing leg before excessive reach. Retain all r33 output coefficients. Paired hidden cancellation preserves zero-command outputs exactly.

plan.hypothesis: Stronger leading-foot inhibition will terminate repeated same-side advancement and promote trailing-leg release, improving placement and alternation without destroying r33's sustained direct-onset motion.
plan.readout: Measure selector reversal relative to foot separation and roll, repeated same-side advances, touchdown-relative X, clearance and support loads. Favor shorter leading-foot excursions followed by qualified opposite-side landings, bounded pelvis height and sustained forward progression. Suppressed release, rapid switching without clearance, or unchanged backward landing collapse rejects the hypothesis. Check whether seed 273 retains its full-horizon stability and whether velocity improves toward 0.50 m/s; distinguish sliding and contact chatter from qualified steps. Assess settled onset and stopping separately.

proposal.diagnosis: r34 rejects doubling separation feedback: seed 273 loses forward velocity by 0.76 seconds and uprightness by 1.70 seconds, versus 20-second upright progression in r33. Early roll and load excursions also increase; stronger algebraic inhibition did not produce effective trailing-leg support. Test magnitude 5 rather than 8, retaining every r34 output and other hidden coefficient. This leaves modestly stronger separation feedback than r33 without restoring that checkpoint. Zero-command cancellation remains exact.

plan.hypothesis: A smaller separation gain will avoid disrupting the early reciprocal motion while retaining some leading-foot inhibition. Whether any improvement over r33 exists between gains 4 and 8 remains unestablished.
plan.readout: Compare the first second's roll, foot loads, forward velocity and bilateral ankle clipping with r34. Require recovery of sustained upright progression in seed 273, then assess qualified alternating runs, touchdown-relative X and speed against r33's approximately 0.20 m/s. In the ramped trial, favor reduced repeated leading-foot advancement followed by supported opposite-side steps. Continued early backward collapse, static double support, or merely delayed failure rejects this compromise. Check settled onset and stopping independently.

proposal.diagnosis: r35 restores 20-second upright progression in seed 273, but produces no qualified touchdowns: frequent releases remain brief and shallow. Settled onset still overruns planted feet, while ramped onset overreaches and falls backward. Rather than further tuning separation gain, add modest knee-angle-difference feedback to the existing selectors. A left knee flexed 0.10 rad more than the right adds +0.15/-0.15 to the left/right hidden arguments, potentially sustaining the selected swing through rapid roll reversals. Retain all r35 coefficients. Matching additions within each hidden pair preserve exact zero-command cancellation.

plan.hypothesis: Feedback from actual knee flexion will provide state-dependent persistence to leg selection, lengthening short unloading intervals enough for genuine swing and support exchange. Excessive persistence could instead lock one leg in flexion or delay weight acceptance.
plan.readout: Measure selector reversals relative to knee-angle difference, roll and contact edges. Compare air duration, clearance, knee extension before landing, opposite-foot support load and pelvis height with r35. Favor repeated qualified alternating touchdowns with sustained forward progression toward 0.50 m/s. Persistent same-side flexion, larger forward reach, bilateral unloading, stronger impacts or loss of the stable seed-273 motion rejects the hypothesis. Evaluate settled onset and stopping separately; displacement without qualified footfalls is insufficient.

proposal.diagnosis: r36 produces qualified releases after settled onset, but strongly amplifies motion rather than establishing controlled swing persistence. Seed 273 lands with feet 0.22–0.30 m ahead within 0.46 seconds and loses uprightness at 0.78 seconds; the ramped trial now fails at 0.25 m/s. Reduce knee-difference coupling fivefold to ±0.3, retaining every other r36 coefficient. A 0.10-rad knee difference will shift each selector by only 0.03 instead of 0.15. This tests weak persistence rather than restoring the zero-coupling checkpoint. Standing cancellation remains exact.

plan.hypothesis: Weak knee-state reinforcement may improve release duration without the rapidly growing excursion caused by gain 1.5. A useful intermediate regime is uncertain.
plan.readout: Compare early knee-angle contrast, roll amplitude, selector timing, air duration and touchdown-relative X against r35 and r36. Favor bounded excursions with qualified alternating landings, retained support height and sustained forward progression toward 0.50 m/s. Growing reach, backward acceleration, simultaneous unloading or renewed early collapse rejects the revision. Returning to r35's unqualified shuffling would indicate insufficient benefit, even if survival improves. Check settled onset and zero-command recovery separately.

proposal.diagnosis: Even weak knee-state reinforcement in r37 destroys the previously sustained direct-onset motion: feet drift ahead, both ankles clip negative, and backward collapse follows. Remove those eight reinforcing coefficients individually and increase knee velocity damping from -0.02 to -0.06. This tests damping rapid knee reversals rather than reinforcing flexion; it does not restore an earlier checkpoint. At 2 rad/s, the damping increment changes the native knee target by approximately -0.092 rad. Unlike paired hidden edits, this affects standing transients and requires explicit regression testing.

plan.hypothesis: Additional knee velocity damping will reduce abrupt flexion-extension reversals and impact-driven oscillation, permitting smoother support exchange after removal of the destabilizing knee-state loop. It may instead suppress swing clearance.
plan.readout: Check full-horizon standing first. During motion, compare knee angular velocities, reversal timing, clearance, air duration, impact loads and vertical pelvis velocity with r35 and r37. Favor slower bounded exchanges with qualified alternating landings and sustained forward progression toward 0.50 m/s. Reduced clearance, planted-foot runaway, backward landing collapse or standing degradation opposes the revision. Recovery of survival alone would not establish a damping benefit; require improved footfall quality relative to r35.

proposal.diagnosis: r38 preserves standing but suppresses useful support replacement: seed 273's feet move from near the pelvis to approximately 0.10 m behind by 3 seconds, followed by positive ankle saturation and forward collapse. Earlier revisions instead failed with feet increasingly ahead. Add common hip feedback proportional to mean foot-relative X: extend when feet lead and flex when they trail. At mean offset ±0.15 m, this changes both native hip targets by ±0.128 rad while preserving their differential target. Retain all r38 coefficients, including knee damping. Standing is not mathematically unchanged and must be retested.

plan.hypothesis: Correcting common fore-aft leg placement from measured support geometry will restrain both trailing-support runaway and excessive forward reach, allowing the existing reciprocal modulation to replace support before ankle saturation dominates.
plan.readout: Track mean foot-relative X, common hip target, actual hip angles, pelvis velocity and ankle clipping before collapse. Favor bounded support offsets with genuine clearance, qualified alternating touchdowns and sustained upright speed approaching 0.50 m/s. Loaded-foot sliding, suppressed release, larger pitch oscillations or unchanged runaway despite corrective targets opposes the hypothesis. Verify full-horizon standing and stopping recovery; bounded double support alone is not walking.

proposal.diagnosis: r39 preserves standing but does not improve support replacement: both walking trials overrun planted feet, and their qualified touchdowns occur after uprightness is lost. Common hip-position correction is therefore insufficient. Increased knee damping in r38 also replaced r35's sustained motion with shrinking foot excursions and forward collapse. Reduce knee velocity damping from -0.06 to -0.03, retaining all r39 placement feedback and other coefficients. This tests whether excessive damping prevents swing completion without restoring an earlier checkpoint.

plan.hypothesis: Lower knee damping will restore enough differential knee motion for actual clearance and forward support replacement while retaining some damping of rapid reversals. Existing hip-position feedback may still destabilize placement.
plan.readout: Compare knee angular velocities, actual knee-angle contrast, clearance, air duration and foot-relative X against r39 during the first three commanded seconds. Favor qualified alternating landings before height loss, bounded support offsets and sustained velocity approaching 0.50 m/s. Growing impacts, backward overreach, continued planted-foot runaway or unqualified shuffling rejects useful improvement. Verify full-horizon standing and stopping recovery.

proposal.diagnosis: r40 prolongs direct-onset progression but still produces no qualified touchdowns; brief releases terminate before useful support replacement, followed by planted-foot forward collapse. Test contact-dependent swing persistence rather than further increasing continuously active gains. During left-only flight, shift the left/right selector arguments by +0.15/-0.15, reversing for right-only flight. The added terms vanish in double support and bilateral flight. Retain all r40 coefficients. Unlike the failed knee-angle reinforcement, this addition acts only during asymmetric contact; paired hidden cancellation also preserves zero-command outputs exactly.

plan.hypothesis: Modest reinforcement of the already airborne leg will lengthen brief release intervals enough for clearance and forward placement, while existing roll and separation feedback still terminate swing. Binary contact feedback could instead amplify chatter or delay supportive landing.
plan.readout: Compare the first release and subsequent 0.20 seconds with r40: selector values, knee targets, clearance, air duration, opposite-foot load and touchdown-relative X. Favor supported, qualified alternating landings followed by sustained upright progression toward 0.50 m/s. Repeated same-side hopping, excessive reach, prolonged unsupported flight, larger impacts or continued unqualified shuffling rejects the hypothesis. Track ankle clipping and pelvis height, and assess stopping recovery separately.

proposal.diagnosis: r41's contact reinforcement causes early forward foot drift and backward motion, not controlled swing persistence: seed 273 is already retreating by 0.50 seconds. Because the selectors drive hips, ankles and lateral transfer as well as knees, this intervention was not isolated to clearance. Remove contact terms from those selectors and introduce contact-conditioned differential knee shortening only. At 0.50 m/s with one foot airborne, the new terms flex its knee and extend the opposite knee by approximately 0.054 rad each. They cancel with equal contacts and at zero command. All other r41 coefficients remain unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Restricting contact-dependent reinforcement to leg-length contrast will improve airborne-foot clearance without simultaneously increasing hip reach or perturbing ankle and lateral commands. It may still delay landing or amplify contact chatter.
plan.readout: Compare knee targets immediately after release, clearance, air duration, opposite support load and touchdown-relative X against r40 and r41. Favor qualified alternating landings with bounded reach, stable height and sustained forward progression toward 0.50 m/s. Backward drift before landing, prolonged same-side flight, impact spikes, chatter or continued planted-foot runaway rejects the hypothesis. Verify that added knee terms cancel at equal contacts and zero command, and measure stopping recovery.

proposal.diagnosis: r42's knee-only contact feedback achieves 20-second upright progression in seed 273 with 30 qualified touchdowns and a longest alternating run of nine. However, speed remains approximately 0.20 m/s, qualified air intervals are only 0.08 seconds, and settled onset still fails to establish stepping. Increase only contact-conditioned knee contrast by 50%, from 0.05 to 0.075. At 0.50 m/s during single support, the added knee flexion/extension becomes approximately ±0.080 rad. Equal-contact and zero-command cancellation remain exact; all other r42 coefficients stay unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Moderately stronger airborne-leg shortening and opposite-leg extension will improve clearance and swing completion, making alternating footfalls more reliable without increasing hip reach directly. It may instead delay landing or amplify vertical oscillations.
plan.readout: Compare clearance, air-duration distributions, qualified alternating runs, support loads and pelvis vertical motion against r42. Favor earlier supported stepping after settled onset and sustained forward speed improving toward 0.50 m/s. Increased reach followed by backward collapse, bilateral unloading, impact spikes or loss of seed 273's sustained gait rejects the increment. Longer survival or more contact edges alone is insufficient. Test stopping from established motion explicitly.

proposal.diagnosis: r43's stronger contact-conditioned knee contrast destroys r42's sustained direct-onset gait: feet progressively lead the pelvis, ankle actions saturate negative, and velocity reverses before collapse. Settled onset now produces early qualified steps but likewise fails during weight acceptance. Retain r43's knee terms and reduce differential hidden hip excursion by 20%, from 0.15 to 0.12, preserving its common component. This tests whether stronger clearance can be retained with less fore-aft reach. All other coefficients remain unchanged, and zero-command hidden cancellation is preserved.

plan.hypothesis: Smaller differential hip excursion will reduce overreaching during the stronger knee-assisted swings, allowing the pelvis to accept the new support rather than retreat behind advancing feet.
plan.readout: Compare touchdown-relative X, mean foot-relative X, ankle clipping and pelvis velocity immediately after landing with r43. Favor retained clearance followed by supported opposite-side steps, stable height and sustained forward speed toward 0.50 m/s. Lost advancement, planted-foot forward runaway, or continued backward collapse despite shorter reach opposes the hypothesis. Require qualified upright alternation, not merely contact edges or longer survival. Test stopping if sustained motion develops.

proposal.diagnosis: r44's smaller hip excursion delays direct-onset collapse but does not prevent backward motion; settled onset again fails without qualified steps. The r43 increase strengthened both airborne-knee flexion and opposite support-knee extension, so its failure cannot be attributed to clearance alone. Retain airborne-side gain 0.075 and reduce only contralateral extension gain to 0.025. At 0.50 m/s during single support, added swing flexion remains approximately 0.082 rad, while support extension falls to approximately 0.025 rad. Zero-command cancellation remains exact; equal-contact additions no longer cancel, but in double support add only approximately 0.002 rad of knee flexion.

plan.hypothesis: Reducing contact-triggered support-leg extension will limit abrupt support impulses and premature unloading while retaining airborne-foot clearance. Conversely, weaker support extension may worsen height retention.
plan.readout: Compare support-knee targets and motion, peak support loads, pelvis vertical velocity, clearance and touchdown-relative X against r44. Favor retained swing clearance with smoother weight acceptance, bounded forward placement and repeated upright alternating steps. Increased sinking, prolonged same-side flight, unchanged backward drift or continued planted-foot runaway rejects the hypothesis. Measure sustained speed against 0.50 m/s and stopping recovery; contact counts alone are insufficient.

proposal.diagnosis: r45's weaker support extension does not resolve either failure mode. Direct onset develops bilateral negative ankle clipping before backward collapse; settled onset still overruns planted feet. The inherited differential ankle modulation pushes the selected flexing leg's ankle target further negative and the opposite target positive. Remove only this modulation to test whether it disrupts clearance or landing acceptance now that contact-conditioned knees provide unloading. Retain all r45 knee, hip, ankle-position and velocity feedback. The removed terms cancel at zero command, so standing outputs remain unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Removing selector-driven ankle modulation will reduce phase-dependent ankle extremes and improve weight acceptance without eliminating knee-generated clearance. Alternatively, that modulation may be essential for release.
plan.readout: Compare ankle commands and angles around release and touchdown, separating position, velocity and removed selector contributions. Favor retained clearance with less clipping, bounded touchdown-relative X, forward weight acceptance and sustained qualified alternation toward 0.50 m/s. Lost release, increased foot sliding, unchanged bilateral clipping or renewed forward runaway rejects the hypothesis. Track pelvis height and velocity rather than interpreting contact counts as success; assess stopping if established motion survives.

proposal.diagnosis: r46 removes ramped-onset stepping without preventing either collapse direction. A remaining competing feedback is common hip pitch: positive pelvis pitch commands hip extension while support trails, and negative pitch commands flexion while feet lead. This may oppose the intended foot-position correction. Reduce only hip root_pitch gain from 0.55 to 0.35, retaining pitch-rate feedback and all other r46 terms. At pitch ±0.10 rad, the change is ∓0.057 rad in each native hip target. This tests a placement-versus-torso-stabilization tradeoff; standing must be retested.

plan.hypothesis: Weaker common hip pitch-angle feedback will reduce reinforcement of fore-aft placement errors during lean, allowing existing foot-position and velocity feedback to retain support beneath the pelvis. Reduced torso stiffness could instead worsen balance.
plan.readout: Separate pitch-angle, pitch-rate, foot-position and velocity contributions to common hip targets. Compare foot-relative X, pitch growth, ankle clipping and post-touchdown pelvis velocity with r46. Favor bounded placement with qualified upright alternation and sustained forward speed approaching 0.50 m/s. Larger torso excursions, standing instability, lost release or unchanged collapse despite corrected hip targets rejects the hypothesis. Evaluate stopping recovery separately from survival.

proposal.diagnosis: r47 contradicts the proposed benefit of weaker hip pitch feedback. In seed 273, pitch reaches -0.144 rad at 2 seconds versus -0.066 in r46, and upright duration falls from 4.44 to 3.14 seconds. Settled onset also develops greater forward pitch without useful stepping. Test stronger pitch stabilization at gain 0.65, above r46's 0.55, while retaining every other r47 coefficient. This tests whether torso stabilization outweighs the apparent placement conflict; it does not restore an earlier checkpoint.

plan.hypothesis: Stronger hip pitch-angle feedback will restrain lean before ankle saturation and support loss, improving weight acceptance during existing foot exchanges. Excessive stiffness could instead suppress release or increase impacts.
plan.readout: Compare pitch and pitch-rate growth during the first two commanded seconds, mean foot-relative X, ankle clipping onset, touchdown loads and post-landing velocity against r47 and r46. Favor bounded torso attitude with retained clearance and sustained qualified alternating progression toward 0.50 m/s. Bounded pitch without support replacement is insufficient; earlier clipping, greater impacts, lost stepping or standing degradation rejects the revision. Assess stopping recovery if motion persists.

proposal.diagnosis: r48 preserves standing but stronger pitch feedback does not improve walking: direct-onset velocity reverses while both feet move ahead, and settled onset still overruns planted support. Stop increasing pitch stiffness. Test additional command-dependent common hip extension, a direction that previously improved sustained progression in r32–r33. Add 0.01 times the sum of the paired selector signals to each hip, approximately +0.055 rad near symmetric activation at 0.50 m/s, while preserving differential gain 0.12. All other r48 coefficients remain unchanged; zero-command outputs are unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: A modest rearward shift of average leg placement will reduce forward foot drift during the existing knee-assisted exchanges, allowing continued forward weight acceptance. It may instead aggravate trailing-support failure after settled onset.
plan.readout: Compare mean foot-relative X, common hip angles, ankle clipping and pelvis velocity during the first three commanded seconds with r48. Favor bounded placement, retained clearance and sustained qualified alternating progression toward 0.50 m/s. Earlier forward runaway, reduced release, increasingly negative pitch or unchanged backward collapse rejects the revision. Require improvement beyond initial displacement and assess stopping from any sustained gait.

proposal.diagnosis: r49's additional hip extension does not arrest forward foot drift or backward collapse during direct onset. Since r43, stronger contact-conditioned knee feedback has remained associated with lost sustained gait; reducing support extension and adjusting hip placement have not resolved it. Reduce only ipsilateral airborne-knee gain from 0.075 to 0.05, retaining contralateral gain -0.025 and every other r49 coefficient. At 0.50 m/s during single support, added swing-knee flexion decreases from approximately 0.082 to 0.055 rad. This isolates excessive swing reinforcement without restoring r42. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Weaker airborne-knee reinforcement will allow earlier supportive extension and reduce accumulating placement error while retaining enough clearance for qualified alternating steps.
plan.readout: Compare knee extension timing before touchdown, air duration, clearance, touchdown-relative X, ankle clipping and post-landing velocity with r49. Favor retained qualified alternation with bounded placement and sustained forward progression toward 0.50 m/s. Lost clearance, renewed planted-foot runaway, unchanged backward drift or improved survival without useful footfalls rejects the hypothesis. Assess stopping if sustained motion develops.

proposal.diagnosis: r50 recovered approximately 0.20 m/s walking and successful stopping for seed 273, but both settled starts remained planted until forward collapse. Test weak reciprocal ankle modulation to assist release: one-third of the previously removed amplitude. Retain every other r50 coefficient; added terms cancel exactly at zero command.

plan.hypothesis: Weak selector-driven ankle modulation will help initiate support exchange from standing without the excessive placement excursions previously associated with stronger modulation.
plan.readout: Compare first-release timing, ankle clipping, clearance, opposite-foot load and touchdown-relative X against r50. Require qualified alternating landings before height loss on settled starts, while preserving seed 273's sustained gait and stopping. Measure commanded-segment speed separately against 0.50 m/s. Backward foot-placement drift, lost sustained gait, continued planted-foot collapse or contact chatter without useful advancement rejects the change.

proposal.diagnosis: r51 retained seed 273's approximately 0.20 m/s gait and stopping, but weak ankle modulation did not establish stepping from settled starts. Increase selector-driven knee contrast by approximately 15%, preserving its common component and all other r51 weights. Unlike stronger contact reinforcement, this acts before liftoff.

plan.hypothesis: Greater reciprocal leg-length contrast will unload one foot sufficiently to initiate supported stepping from double support, without increasing average commanded knee flexion or prolonging contact-triggered swing reinforcement.
plan.readout: Compare pre-liftoff knee contrast, foot loads, first-release timing, clearance and subsequent support acceptance with r51. Favor qualified alternating touchdowns before height loss after settled onset, while retaining sustained direct-start walking and stopping. Track commanded-segment speed against 0.50 m/s. Increased vertical impulses, simultaneous unloading, backward placement drift, lost sustained gait or merely delayed planted-foot collapse rejects the change. Verify full-horizon standing.

proposal.diagnosis: r52's stronger knee contrast failed to initiate settled stepping and lost sustained direct-start walking. Knee amplitude alone did not resolve unloading. Test stronger coordinated lateral hip modulation while retaining every other r52 coefficient; the edit cancels exactly at zero command.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing lateral modulation from 0.26 to 0.30 will improve weight transfer onto the supporting foot, allowing existing knee shortening to produce useful release rather than loaded-leg motion. It may instead amplify roll and destabilize support.
plan.readout: Compare lateral pelvis motion, roll, opposite-foot load and knee motion before first release against r52. Require supported liftoff and qualified alternating landings before height loss after settled onset. In direct-start walking, track sustained speed toward 0.50 m/s, touchdown-relative X and ankle clipping. Growing lateral excursions, bilateral unloading, backward drift or continued planted-foot collapse rejects the hypothesis. Verify standing and stopping separately; collapse-associated touchdowns do not count as improvement.

proposal.diagnosis: r53 preserved standing but did not improve settled initiation and shortened direct-start survival. Both walking failure modes retain large common foot offsets and bilateral ankle saturation. Reduce common ankle foot-position gain from -12 to -10 while preserving differential gain -6; leave all other r53 weights unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Moderately weaker common foot-position feedback will reduce ankle saturation as both feet move ahead of or behind the pelvis, permitting corrective support exchange. It could instead weaken essential standing stabilization or increase sliding.
plan.readout: Compare mean foot-relative X, unclipped ankle contributions, clipping duration, pitch growth and post-touchdown velocity against r53. Require bounded support offsets and qualified upright alternation, not merely reduced clipping or longer survival. Measure walking-segment speed toward 0.50 m/s. Standing drift, increased sliding, lost clearance or persistent forward/backward collapse opposes the change. Test stopping if sustained walking survives.

proposal.diagnosis: r54 retained standing but accelerated settled-start forward collapse; direct-start stepping still ended in backward collapse. Reduced position feedback did not bound support geometry. Increase ankle forward-velocity feedback from 3.5 to 4.2, retaining every other r54 coefficient, to test whether earlier velocity-dependent correction arrests divergence.

plan.hypothesis: Stronger ankle velocity feedback will oppose developing forward and backward motion before support offsets become unrecoverable. It may instead suppress useful progression or cause earlier saturation.
plan.readout: Compare ankle velocity contributions, clipping onset, pelvis acceleration, mean foot-relative X and post-landing velocity with r54. Favor bounded motion with repeated qualified upright alternation and retained support height. Reduced speed or longer survival alone is insufficient: report walking-segment speed against 0.50 m/s. Earlier saturation, stationary shuffling, lost release, unchanged collapse or standing degradation rejects useful improvement. Assess stopping separately.

proposal.diagnosis: r55 preserved standing but reduced early direct-start speed and advanced backward collapse from 9.58 to 3.14 seconds. Increasing velocity feedback alone also changed its balance with command drive. Strengthen ankle command feedforward while retaining the 4.2 velocity gain and every other r55 coefficient.

plan.hypothesis: Stronger command drive will restore forward weight acceptance during stepping while retaining the increased velocity feedback. The command-to-velocity gain ratio becomes approximately 0.38, close to r54's 0.37. It may instead worsen planted-foot forward collapse or negative ankle saturation.
plan.readout: Compare early forward speed, post-landing acceleration, mean foot-relative X and ankle clipping against r55 and r54. Favor sustained qualified upright alternation with bounded placement and speed improving toward 0.50 m/s. Earlier settled-start runaway, increased backward drift, lost clearance or saturation without useful progression rejects the change. Distinguish walking-segment speed from whole-trial averages and verify stopping recovery.

proposal.diagnosis: r56 modestly prolonged direct-start stepping but retained backward collapse and worsened settled-start forward collapse. More drive did not produce support replacement. Test selector timing rather than further amplitude increases: reduce roll-rate sensitivity from 0.06 to 0.04, retaining all other r56 weights. Zero-command paired cancellation remains intact.

plan.hypothesis: Weaker roll-rate input will reduce premature selector reversals during unloading, allowing longer supported swings and more complete weight transfer. It may instead delay necessary switching and cause overreach or excessive roll.
plan.readout: Compare selector reversal timing relative to roll, liftoff and touchdown with r56. Measure air duration, clearance, opposite-foot load, touchdown-relative X and post-landing velocity. Favor qualified alternating support replacement before height loss, bounded excursions and sustained speed approaching 0.50 m/s. Longer flight without weight acceptance, repeated same-side steps, bilateral unloading or unchanged planted-foot collapse rejects the hypothesis. Verify standing and stopping separately.

proposal.diagnosis: Reducing selector roll-rate sensitivity worsened direct-start backward collapse: upright duration fell from 4.48 to 1.86 seconds without longer useful swings. Settled initiation remained unsuccessful. Test sensitivity 0.08, above r56's 0.06, while retaining all other r57 weights.

plan.hypothesis: Stronger anticipatory selector switching will limit accumulating forward foot placement and improve timely support acceptance. Excessive rate sensitivity may instead suppress release and leave both feet planted.
plan.readout: Compare selector reversals, knee-target contrast, touchdown-relative X and post-landing pelvis velocity against r57 and r56. Require bounded placement with qualified alternating support exchanges before height loss and sustained progression toward 0.50 m/s. Suppressed clearance, contact chatter, stationary double support or unchanged collapse rejects useful improvement, even if survival increases. Verify standing and stopping independently.

proposal.diagnosis: r58 recovered sustained direct-start stepping at approximately 0.19 m/s and successful stopping, but settled onset still remained planted until forward collapse. Test a small command-dependent lateral bias to initiate weight transfer. At 0.50 m/s it adds 0.04 normalized hip-roll command; all other r58 weights remain unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: A modest lateral bias will move settled double support into the existing stepping regime without requiring larger reciprocal excursions. Because the bias persists during walking, it may instead cause one-sided stepping or lateral drift.
plan.readout: Compare the first commanded second with r58: lateral pelvis displacement, foot-load difference, selector contrast and supported liftoff. Require qualified alternating landings before height loss on settled onset, not merely earlier contact edges. Check whether direct-start stepping and stopping remain stable, and measure walking-segment speed against 0.50 m/s. Persistent side preference, growing lateral drift, backward overreach or unchanged planted-foot collapse rejects the hypothesis. Zero-command outputs should remain unchanged.

proposal.diagnosis: r59 failed to initiate settled stepping and introduced accumulating lateral drift and yaw during direct-start walking. Replace its persistent lateral bias with a stronger low-speed bias that attenuates as forward velocity develops. Retain all other r59 coefficients; the new paired terms cancel exactly at zero command.

plan.hypothesis: A larger initial weight-transfer stimulus, followed by velocity-dependent attenuation, will initiate stepping without continuously steering established walking. At command 0.50, the added normalized hip-roll command is approximately 0.077 at rest and 0.002 at 0.18 m/s.
plan.readout: Measure the new hidden-pair contribution, initial foot-load redistribution, supported liftoff and qualified alternating landings after settled onset. During direct-start motion, check whether lateral drift and yaw stop accumulating as the bias attenuates. Require sustained upright progression toward 0.50 m/s, not merely a transient release. Persistent low-speed bias, one-sided stepping, backward collapse or continued planted-foot runaway rejects the hypothesis. Verify standing cancellation and stopping recovery.

proposal.diagnosis: r60 eliminated accumulating lateral drift and retained direct-start walking and stopping, but settled initiation remained unchanged. Test slightly greater command-dependent common knee flexion, preserving reciprocal contrast and all other r60 weights. Near symmetric 0.50 command, this adds approximately 0.045 rad to each knee target; standing commands remain unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: A modestly more flexed commanded posture will facilitate release from settled double support and reduce dependence on reset transients. It may instead consume support-height margin or worsen forward foot placement.
plan.readout: Compare early knee angles, pelvis height, foot-load redistribution and supported liftoff against r60. Require qualified upright alternating steps after settled onset, with bounded foot-relative X and sustained speed toward 0.50 m/s. Sinking, bilateral unloading, backward drift or unchanged planted-foot collapse rejects the hypothesis. Test restart after a successful stop to distinguish reset-dependent stepping from repeatable initiation.

proposal.diagnosis: r61 preserved standing and demonstrated stopping and restarting on seed 273, but progression remained approximately 0.18 m/s with sparse, right-dominated qualified steps. Seed 272 still collapsed without useful support replacement. Increased common flexion lowered walking height without resolving settled initiation. Retain r61 and test low-speed reciprocal knee assistance rather than further common flexion.

plan.hypothesis: Adding left-knee flexion and equal right-knee extension through the existing low-speed command gate will initiate supported unilateral release. The added knee contrast attenuates as forward speed develops and cancels exactly at zero command. It may instead produce excessive asymmetric loading or repeated same-side steps.
plan.readout: Compare the first commanded second against r61: gate contribution, knee-angle difference, foot loads, clearance and supported liftoff. Require qualified alternating support replacement before height loss on seed 272, while preserving seed 273's walking, stopping and restart. Measure each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s, touchdown-relative X, lateral drift and ankle clipping. Reject bilateral unloading, persistent side preference, backward drift or unchanged planted-foot collapse; collapse-associated touchdowns and survival alone are insufficient.

proposal.diagnosis: r62 changed the initial releasing foot on seed 272 but produced only 0.04 s of flight, followed by unchanged planted-foot collapse. Seed 273 retained progression and restart but lost qualified alternation entirely. Test whether coordinating the existing low-speed knee assistance with fore-aft hip motion converts brief unloading into support replacement. All other r62 weights remain unchanged.

plan.hypothesis: Low-speed left-hip flexion and right-hip extension will advance the shortened left leg while retaining contralateral support. This assistance attenuates with forward speed and cancels at zero command. It may instead increase overreach or reinforce one-sided stepping.
plan.readout: Compare initial liftoff, airborne foot advancement, clearance, opposite-foot load and landing-relative X with r62. Require supported alternating landings before height loss on settled onset, and recovery of qualified alternation during direct start and restart. Measure walking-segment speed against 0.50 m/s separately from stopping. Reject increased forward foot drift, backward deceleration, persistent side preference, bilateral unloading or unchanged planted-foot collapse. Standing and stopping must remain upright.
