proposal.diagnosis: r63's forward-placement assistance destroyed direct-start progression: speed reversed before 0.76 s, both feet accumulated ahead of the pelvis, and collapse occurred at 2.20 s. Settled initiation remained unsuccessful. From r63, reverse and halve only the gated hip-pitch assistance; retain all other weights.

plan.hypothesis: Mild retraction of the shortened left leg, with opposite right-hip motion, will limit premature forward placement during unloading and preserve forward weight acceptance. It may instead prevent useful swing advancement or worsen trailing-foot support.
plan.readout: Compare early foot-relative X, hip angles, pelvis velocity and ankle saturation with r63 and r62. Require supported release followed by qualified alternating landings, not merely recovery of upright shuffling. Check settled initiation, direct-start progression and restart separately. Measure walking-segment speed against 0.50 m/s. Reject backward drift, trailing-foot runaway, persistent side preference or lost clearance. Verify zero-command standing cancellation and stopping stability.

proposal.diagnosis: r64 recovered initial forward progression but produced no qualified steps before stopping; restart then failed through planted-foot forward collapse. Settled initiation also remained unsuccessful. The initiation gate attenuates with pelvis translation even without support replacement. Retain all r64 output weights and test slower velocity-dependent attenuation.

plan.hypothesis: Extending the existing coordinated initiation assistance into early forward motion will allow brief unloading to develop into useful support exchange. Initial assistance remains unchanged and zero-command cancellation is preserved. Longer-lived asymmetry may instead cause side preference, yaw drift or overreach.
plan.readout: Compare gate contribution, foot-load redistribution, flight duration and airborne advancement during the first commanded second against r64. Require qualified upright alternating landings after settled onset and restart, with bounded foot-relative X. Track lateral drift, yaw, ankle clipping and walking-segment speed against 0.50 m/s. Reject persistent unilateral stepping, backward drift, continued planted-foot collapse or survival without qualified alternation. Verify standing and both stopping transitions.

proposal.diagnosis: r65 prolonged asymmetry without improving settled initiation; direct-start motion developed substantial lateral and yaw drift before collapse. Qualified alternation had already deteriorated when gated knee assistance was introduced in r62. Remove only that assistance to isolate its contribution, retaining r65's gate, hip assistance and all other coefficients.

plan.hypothesis: Removing the fixed-side knee contrast will let the reciprocal selectors govern leg shortening and support exchange, reducing persistent loading asymmetry. Retained hip assistance may still initiate weight transfer, but release could instead become weaker.
plan.readout: Compare knee contrast, left/right loading, roll, yaw and lateral velocity against r65 during the first three commanded seconds. Require recovered qualified upright alternation with bounded foot placement, not merely reduced drift or longer survival. Test settled initiation and restart independently; report walking-segment speed against 0.50 m/s. Unchanged planted-foot collapse, lost clearance, continued side preference or backward drift rejects useful improvement. Verify standing and stopping.

proposal.diagnosis: r66 retained right-only qualified stepping before the first stop, accumulated yaw to approximately -0.20 rad, and collapsed backward after restart. Settled initiation remained unsuccessful. Remove only the remaining gated lateral bias to test whether it obstructs balanced support exchange; retain r66's gated hip-pitch terms and all other weights.

plan.hypothesis: Removing fixed-direction lateral assistance will reduce accumulated heading and loading asymmetry, allowing reciprocal modulation to produce bilateral qualified steps and a more stable restart. It may instead weaken initial unloading without correcting placement.
plan.readout: Compare left/right flight duration, clearance, foot loads, yaw and lateral displacement with r66 before the first stop. Require qualified upright alternation, bounded touchdown-relative X and successful support replacement after restart. Evaluate settled initiation separately and report walking-segment speed against 0.50 m/s. Reduced drift without useful steps, unchanged planted-foot collapse, backward overreach or lost stopping stability rejects useful improvement. Verify standing cancellation.

proposal.diagnosis: r67 sustained approximately 0.18–0.19 m/s initially, but its short contact exchanges produced no qualified touchdowns. Settled onset and restart still ended in planted-foot collapse. Test a small reduction in selector rate sensitivity, retaining every other r67 coefficient. Earlier deterioration at 0.04 argues against a large reduction.

plan.hypothesis: Reducing roll-rate sensitivity from 0.08 to 0.07 will delay premature selector reversals enough for supported swings to achieve useful clearance and advancement. It may instead permit overreach and backward instability.
plan.readout: Compare selector reversals relative to liftoff, flight duration, clearance, opposite-foot load and touchdown-relative X against r67. Require repeated qualified upright alternation with bounded placement, not merely longer flight or threshold-crossing touchdowns. Measure walking-segment speed toward 0.50 m/s and post-landing velocity. Test settled initiation and restart separately. Reject accumulating forward foot placement, backward deceleration, bilateral unloading or unchanged planted-foot collapse. Verify standing and stopping.

proposal.diagnosis: r68 recovered some qualified alternation during initial motion, but settled onset and restart still produced growing trailing-foot offsets and forward collapse. Test stronger common foot-position feedback at the hips rather than additional initiation bias. Retain every other r68 coefficient.

plan.hypothesis: Stronger positive common foot-position feedback will flex the hips when both feet trail the pelvis and extend them when both feet lie ahead, limiting placement drift and enabling support replacement. It may instead disturb standing or suppress useful stride motion.
plan.readout: Compare mean foot-relative X, common hip angle, pitch, ankle clipping and supported release against r68 during settled onset and restart. Require bounded placement with repeated qualified upright alternating landings, not merely delayed collapse. During initial walking, assess clearance, post-landing velocity and segment speed toward 0.50 m/s. Reject standing drift, reduced advancement, backward instability, sliding or continued planted-foot collapse. Verify both stopping transitions.

proposal.diagnosis: r69 changed torso posture without resolving trailing-foot collapse after settled onset or restart. Initial motion retained short exchanges but no qualified alternation. From r69, modestly increase only own-foot airborne knee reinforcement; retain all other weights.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing airborne reinforcement from 0.05 to 0.06 will prevent premature recontact after initial unloading and provide enough clearance for useful support exchange. Earlier failures at 0.075 caution against a larger increase. Excess reinforcement could delay weight acceptance or cause forward overreach.
plan.readout: Compare knee motion immediately after liftoff, flight duration, clearance, opposite-foot load and touchdown-relative X against r69. Require qualified upright alternating landings with maintained post-landing forward velocity, including after settled onset and restart. Report walking-segment speed against 0.50 m/s. Reject bilateral unloading, increasing forward foot offsets, backward deceleration, prolonged flight without support acceptance or unchanged planted-foot collapse. Verify standing and stopping.

proposal.diagnosis: r70 did not improve settled initiation. During direct-start motion, yaw grew to 0.53 rad by 7 s alongside lateral drift and asymmetric foot placement, followed by stopping failure. Test stronger heading correction while retaining every other r70 coefficient.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing hip-yaw angle feedback will restrain accumulated turning and reduce contamination of world-frame foot-position feedback by heading error. This may preserve balanced support exchange and stopping, but could instead twist planted feet or increase slip.
plan.readout: Compare yaw growth, lateral displacement, hip-yaw angles, planted-foot slip and left/right touchdown placement against r70. Require bounded heading together with qualified upright alternation and sustained progression toward 0.50 m/s; heading improvement alone is insufficient. Check settled onset and restart independently. Reject increased torsional motion, lost clearance, unchanged planted-foot collapse or stopping instability. Measure standing drift and walking-segment speed separately.

proposal.diagnosis: r71 improved initial heading control and survived the first stop, but qualified alternation remained sparse. Settled onset still accelerated over planted feet into collapse. Test reduced low-speed ankle command drive while retaining full command activation of the stepping selectors and every existing r71 coefficient.

plan.hypothesis: Adding positive ankle input through the existing low-speed gate will temper forward drive before support exchange develops. At rest with command 0.50, it offsets approximately 0.386 of the -0.8 command contribution; the offset attenuates with speed and cancels at zero command. It may instead stall progression or provoke backward drift.
plan.readout: Compare the first two commanded seconds against r71: pelvis acceleration, mean foot-relative X, ankle clipping, foot loads and first supported release. Require qualified alternating support replacement before substantial lean or height loss, followed by sustained progression toward 0.50 m/s. Stationary double support, reduced speed alone, backward placement drift or unchanged planted-foot collapse rejects useful improvement. Assess initial walking, settled onset, restart and stopping separately.

proposal.diagnosis: r72 enabled settled initiation and stopping: seed 272 completed 20 seconds with 13 qualified touchdowns and eight alternations, but walking speed remained approximately 0.16 m/s. Direct start still developed turning and backward motion before stopping. Remove only the fixed-side hip-pitch assistance; retain the successful ankle gating and all other r72 coefficients.

plan.hypothesis: The remaining low-speed hip-pitch asymmetry may bias foot placement and accumulate heading error. Removing it while retaining symmetric ankle gating may preserve settled initiation and improve bilateral support exchange. It could instead weaken initiation or leave turning unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare initial foot-position asymmetry, left/right clearance, qualified touchdown balance, yaw and lateral drift against r72. Require preservation of seed 272's supported initiation and stopping, plus repeated upright alternation during direct start and restart. Report speed separately for each walking segment against 0.50 m/s. Reject renewed planted-foot collapse, backward drift, lost clearance or reduced turning without useful support exchange. Verify unchanged zero-command standing.

proposal.diagnosis: Removing hip-pitch assistance improved direct-start survival through stopping, but lost r72's settled initiation: seed 272 developed backward motion and fell at 5.98 seconds. Restart also collapsed backward; its alternating touchdowns did not establish stable walking. Test half-strength assistance, retaining every other r73 coefficient.

plan.hypothesis: Half-strength low-speed hip-pitch assistance may provide enough initial placement bias to avoid backward overreach while reducing the turning seen with full-strength assistance. The stable initiation range may instead be narrow or absent.
plan.readout: Compare the first two commanded seconds with r72 and r73: foot-relative X, pelvis velocity, pitch, opposite-foot load and landing placement. Require sustained qualified upright alternation after settled onset and restart, not alternating touchdowns during collapse. Check whether direct-start yaw and lateral drift remain bounded through stopping. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s. Reject backward deceleration, renewed planted-foot runaway, persistent unilateral stepping or stopping failure. Verify unchanged standing.

proposal.diagnosis: r74 avoided immediate settled collapse but produced no qualified alternation in either walking trial. Both developed turning and backward instability before stopping. The earlier increase in airborne knee reinforcement also degraded support exchange. Reduce that reinforcement alone, retaining r74's ankle gating and half-strength hip assistance.

plan.hypothesis: Reducing own-foot airborne knee reinforcement from 0.06 to 0.05 may improve timely extension and weight acceptance, reducing asymmetric landings and accumulated turning. With ankle gating retained, initiation may remain viable. Clearance could instead become insufficient.
plan.readout: Compare knee extension before touchdown, flight duration, clearance, landing loads, post-landing forward velocity and yaw growth against r74. Require repeated qualified upright alternation after settled onset and during direct start, followed by stable stopping and restart. Report walking-segment speed against 0.50 m/s. Reject reduced clearance, persistent same-side qualification, backward placement drift or longer survival without useful support exchange. Verify unchanged standing.

proposal.diagnosis: r75 preserved standing and the first direct-start stop, but settled onset reverted to planted-foot collapse. Direct walking remained approximately 0.16 m/s with sparse alternation and accumulated heading error; restart fell backward. Test stronger yaw-rate damping without changing initiation or swing coefficients.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing hip-yaw rate feedback from 0.15 to 0.30 may damp step-induced turning before heading error distorts world-frame foot-placement feedback. It may instead increase planted-foot torsion or interfere with support exchange; settled initiation may remain unresolved.
plan.readout: Compare yaw-rate excursions, net yaw change per support exchange, hip-yaw saturation, planted-foot slip and lateral drift against r75. Require bounded heading together with repeated qualified upright alternation and stable stopping/restart, not heading improvement alone. Measure each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s. Track settled onset separately; reject increased slip, lost clearance, backward overreach or continued collapse. Check standing drift because this edit does not cancel at zero command.

proposal.diagnosis: r76's larger yaw-rate gain induced oscillating, saturated yaw targets even during standing. Foot separation grew beyond 1 m and pelvis height dropped to 0.872 m. Its settled-start comparison was therefore confounded by an already disturbed stance. Reduce only this gain to 0.18, retaining all other r76 weights.

plan.hypothesis: A smaller increase over the formerly stable 0.15 gain may retain some walking heading control without exciting standing torsional oscillations. It may still destabilize stance or provide insufficient heading correction.
plan.readout: First compare standing yaw-target oscillation, clipping, foot separation, slip and height against r75 and r76. Require recovery of stable stance, not upright torso orientation alone. During walking, measure yaw drift, qualified alternating support exchanges and segment speed against 0.50 m/s. Evaluate settled initiation, stopping and restart separately. Reject persistent standing oscillation, backward overreach, planted-foot collapse or heading improvement without useful alternation; exclude collapse-associated touchdowns from evidence of progress.

proposal.diagnosis: r77 recovered stable standing and completed direct start, stopping and restart, but produced only four qualified touchdowns at roughly 0.16 m/s. Settled onset still fell backward. Test intermediate airborne knee reinforcement while retaining r77's yaw feedback and all other weights.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing own-foot airborne reinforcement from 0.05 to 0.055 may turn marginal-clearance swings into reliable support exchanges without the delayed acceptance and turning previously observed at 0.06. It could instead worsen forward foot placement and backward instability.
plan.readout: Compare clearance, flight duration, knee extension before landing, opposite-foot load and post-landing velocity against r77. Require repeated qualified upright alternation during both walking segments while preserving stopping and restart. Assess settled initiation separately: advancing feet accompanied by backward pelvis motion is failure, not progress. Report walking-segment speed against 0.50 m/s, heading drift and ankle clipping. Reject overreach, bilateral unloading, renewed turning or additional touchdowns without stable weight acceptance. Verify unchanged standing.

proposal.diagnosis: r78 completed all trials upright, including settled initiation and restart, but walking remained approximately 0.16 m/s with sparse, mostly unilateral qualified touchdowns. Test modestly stronger forward drive after motion develops while approximately preserving the ankle command at rest.

plan.hypothesis: At target 0.50 and zero forward velocity, the increased gate contribution offsets the additional -0.05 ankle command. As velocity rises and the gate attenuates, stronger forward drive emerges. This may improve progression and support exchange without disrupting initiation, or instead cause planted-foot acceleration and collapse. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Verify approximately unchanged initial ankle targets, then compare acceleration, gate attenuation, foot-relative X, ankle clipping and post-landing velocity against r78. Require increased walking-segment speed toward 0.50 m/s together with repeated qualified upright alternation and preserved stopping/restart. Reject faster motion caused by sliding or falling, trailing-foot runaway, backward overreach, increased heading drift or loss of settled initiation. Assess each walking segment separately and verify standing.

proposal.diagnosis: r79 preserved all three horizons and improved qualified touchdown counts and alternation. Settled walking averaged approximately 0.17 m/s, still far below 0.50. Repeat the same small increase in motion-dependent ankle drive, retaining every other r79 coefficient.

plan.hypothesis: Another compensated increase in ankle command may further improve forward progression and bilateral support exchange. Initial ankle output at target 0.50 and zero velocity remains approximately unchanged; additional forward drive appears as velocity increases. This benefit may saturate or give way to unstable acceleration.
plan.readout: Compare walking-segment speed, qualified alternation frequency, clearance, post-landing velocity and foot-relative X against r79. Require faster upright progression with more consistent bilateral support replacement, while preserving settled initiation, stopping and restart. Track ankle clipping, heading and lateral drift. Reject sliding, trailing-foot runaway, backward overreach or increased speed without useful footfalls. Verify unchanged standing; do not use whole-trial mean speed as the walking readout.

proposal.diagnosis: r80 improved direct-start progression and retained stopping/restart, but settled onset developed overreach and backward collapse. Test intermediate ankle drive between r79 and r80, retaining every other r80 coefficient.

plan.hypothesis: Intermediate motion-dependent drive may retain some speed benefit without triggering r80's settled-onset instability. Initial ankle output at target 0.50 and zero velocity remains approximately unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare early landing-relative X, post-landing velocity, pitch and ankle clipping against r79 and r80. Require sustained qualified upright alternation, preserved stopping/restart and walking-segment speed improvement toward 0.50 m/s. Reject increasing overreach, backward deceleration, sliding or alternating touchdowns during collapse. Verify unchanged standing.

proposal.diagnosis: r81 preserved standing but failed backward after settled onset and forward after restart. Intermediate ankle drive did not produce robust initiation. Direct walking remained about 0.18 m/s with sparse qualified exchanges. Test stronger differential knee unloading rather than further tuning ankle drive; inherit all unlisted r81 weights.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing reciprocal knee contrast from 0.464 to 0.484 while preserving the common coefficient sum of 0.204 may improve swing release and opposite-leg support before liftoff. Unlike airborne reinforcement, this acts during initial unloading. It could instead amplify rocking, overreach or impact loads. Paired cancellation preserves zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare pre-liftoff knee motion, opposite-foot load, clearance, touchdown-relative X and post-landing pelvis velocity against r81. Require repeated upright alternating support acceptance, not contact chatter or collapse-associated touchdowns. Assess settled onset and restart independently; reject backward deceleration, planted-foot forward runaway, bilateral unloading or increased impact without sustained progression. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s, heading drift and ankle clipping. Verify standing and stopping.

proposal.diagnosis: r82 recovered settled initiation and stopping, but qualified alternation remained sparse. Restart developed yaw 0.503 rad, asymmetric foot placement and backward velocity before the stop command. Test stronger heading-angle feedback while retaining r82's knee revision and yaw-rate gain.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing hip-yaw angle feedback from 1.5 to 1.8 may restrain accumulated heading error before it distorts world-frame foot-position feedback. Keeping rate feedback at 0.18 avoids repeating the standing oscillations observed at 0.30. Stronger angle feedback could nevertheless increase planted-foot torsion or saturation.
plan.readout: Compare yaw growth, lateral drift, foot-relative X asymmetry, hip-yaw clipping and planted-foot slip against r82, particularly during restart before 17 seconds. Require bounded heading together with repeated qualified upright alternating support acceptance and preserved forward velocity. Report walking-segment speeds against 0.50 m/s; heading improvement or survival alone is insufficient. Reject increased torsional oscillation, overreach, backward deceleration or lost clearance. Check standing height, foot separation and drift because this edit remains active at zero command.

proposal.diagnosis: r83 preserved standing and settled walking, but restart still accumulated heading error and lost forward velocity before stopping. World-frame foot-X separation can bias the reciprocal selectors when the robot turns. Retain all r83 weights and test first-order heading compensation in those selectors.

plan.hypothesis: At approximately 0.45 m foot separation, yaw contributes about +2.25 times yaw to h0/h1's foot-X term and the opposite to h2/h3. Counteracting this contribution may prevent heading error from imposing a persistent swing-side bias. This is only a small-angle approximation and could weaken useful phase information. Matching each commanded/uncommanded pair preserves cancellation at zero command.
plan.readout: Compare selector imbalance, bilateral clearance, qualified alternation, touchdown placement and yaw growth against r83, especially after restart. Require repeated upright support replacement with maintained forward velocity, not merely smaller heading error. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s and distinguish foot advance from planted-foot slip. Reject phase locking, reduced clearance, overreach, backward deceleration or renewed initiation failure. Verify standing and both stops.

proposal.diagnosis: Full selector heading compensation eliminated qualified footfalls and restored planted-foot forward collapse after settled onset and restart. The geometric correction also altered useful gait-phase dynamics. Reduce compensation to one-third strength; retain every other r84 coefficient.

plan.hypothesis: Partial compensation may preserve the unloading and clearance lost in r84 while reducing the accumulated heading-dependent bias seen in r83. A fixed-width geometric correction may be inappropriate even at reduced strength. Paired cancellation still preserves zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare first-second unloading, selector excursions, flight duration, clearance and opposite-foot load against r84. Require recovery of qualified upright bilateral support exchange after settled onset and restart, followed by bounded heading and stable stopping. Compare later yaw drift against r83. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s. Reject planted-foot acceleration, contact chatter without clearance, backward overreach or heading improvement without useful footfalls. Verify standing remains unchanged.

proposal.diagnosis: r85 retained standing and approximately 0.18 m/s direct progression, but produced no qualified footfalls and failed forward after settled onset and restart. Reduced heading compensation did not restore sufficient unloading. Retain it and test increased knee contrast, inheriting all other r85 weights.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing reciprocal knee contrast from 0.484 to 0.504, with common coefficient sum unchanged at 0.204, may recover clearance and support exchange under the compensated selectors. The earlier contrast increase helped settled initiation, but this increase could instead amplify rocking or landing impacts. Zero-command contributions still cancel.
plan.readout: Compare pre-liftoff knee motion, foot loads, clearance, flight duration and landing-relative X against r85. Require qualified alternating landings followed by sustained forward pelvis motion, not brief contact chatter or sliding. Check whether settled onset and restart escape planted double support before pitch and ankle saturation grow. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s, heading drift and impact loads. Reject bilateral unloading, overreach, backward deceleration or increased clearance without weight acceptance. Verify standing and stopping.

proposal.diagnosis: r86 recovered both walking trials, stopping and restart while preserving standing. Walking averaged approximately 0.17–0.18 m/s, with sparse qualified footfalls and marginal clearance. Test whether another small increase in knee contrast improves reliable bilateral support exchange; retain all other r86 weights.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing reciprocal knee contrast from 0.504 to 0.524 while preserving the common sum of 0.204 may lengthen useful unloading and improve clearance without additional ankle drive. Benefits may saturate or reverse through excessive rocking, delayed weight acceptance or harder landings. Zero-command contributions remain cancelled.
plan.readout: Compare clearance distributions for both feet, flight duration, opposite-foot support load, touchdown-relative X and post-landing velocity against r86. Require more frequent consecutive qualified upright alternating exchanges, not merely additional same-side touchdowns. Measure walking-segment speed against 0.50 m/s and preserve settled initiation, restart and stopping. Reject bilateral unloading, overreach, increased impacts, heading drift or falling/sliding acceleration. Verify unchanged standing.

proposal.diagnosis: r87's additional knee contrast did not improve speed or reliable clearance: settled walking had only two qualified right landings, and restart ended in planted-foot forward collapse. Test selector timing rather than further increasing knee amplitude. Retain all other r87 weights.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing roll-rate input from magnitude 0.07 to 0.08 may advance reciprocal activation during lateral motion, allowing unloading and support transfer before the feet become persistently planted. It could instead shorten swings or amplify rocking. Matching commanded/uncommanded pairs preserves zero-command cancellation.
plan.readout: Compare selector reversals relative to roll, foot unloading and touchdown against r87. Measure bilateral flight duration, clearance, opposite-foot load and post-landing velocity. Require repeated qualified upright alternation during settled onset and restart, not contact chatter or extra touchdowns during collapse. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s, ankle saturation, pitch and heading drift. Reject premature recontact, bilateral unloading, overreach or planted-foot acceleration. Verify standing and stopping.

proposal.diagnosis: r88 preserved direct-start survival and restart but produced no qualified footfalls; settled initiation still collapsed forward. Selector heading compensation has repeatedly reduced useful clearance. Remove those four coefficients while retaining r88's knee contrast, roll-rate input and all other weights—not restoring an earlier checkpoint.

plan.hypothesis: Removing selector yaw compensation may restore useful phase excursions and unloading under the current knee contrast and roll-rate feedback. Dedicated hip-yaw feedback remains active. Clearance could recover at the cost of renewed heading drift or overreach; zero-command cancellation remains intact.
plan.readout: Compare selector excursions, unloading, bilateral clearance and flight duration against r88. Require qualified alternating support acceptance with positive post-landing pelvis velocity during both settled onset and restart. Track yaw and lateral drift to test the cost of removing compensation. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s. Reject contact chatter, persistent same-side stepping, planted-foot acceleration, backward overreach or survival without useful footfalls. Verify standing and stopping.

proposal.diagnosis: r89 recovered all three horizons, but direct-start and restart walking qualified only right-foot landings. Progression remains approximately 0.17–0.18 m/s. Test slightly stronger airborne knee reinforcement for marginal swings while retaining every other r89 weight.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing own-foot contact-gated knee reinforcement from 0.055 to 0.060 may prevent premature recontact and improve bilateral clearance. Its much smaller contribution during contact limits changes to initial unloading. Earlier mixed results at 0.060 caution that it could instead delay weight acceptance or increase overreach. Zero-command contributions cancel.
plan.readout: Compare both feet's clearance and flight-duration distributions, including unqualified swings, against r89. Check knee extension before touchdown, opposite-foot support load and post-landing forward velocity. Require recurring upright left-right support acceptance rather than more right-only qualifications or contact chatter. Report walking-segment speeds against 0.50 m/s. Reject delayed acceptance, bilateral unloading, overreach, heading growth or initiation/restart failure. Verify standing and stopping.

proposal.diagnosis: r90's airborne reinforcement did not establish reliable alternation; both walking trials developed turning and backward instability. Test heading compensation at the ankle outputs rather than the selectors, where compensation previously suppressed useful footfalls. Retain all other r90 weights.

plan.hypothesis: With roughly 0.45 m foot separation, the ankle foot-X terms acquire approximately opposite 1.35-times-yaw contributions during turning. Half-strength counterterms may reduce heading-induced ankle imbalance without directly changing selector timing. This small-angle approximation could instead impair balance or increase foot slip.
plan.readout: Compare left-right ankle target imbalance, clipping, touchdown placement, planted-foot slip and yaw growth against r90. Require preserved clearance plus recurring upright alternating support acceptance, with positive post-landing forward velocity. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s. Reject heading improvement without useful footfalls, increased slip, backward overreach or initiation/restart failure. Check standing drift and foot separation because the new inputs remain active at zero command; verify both stops.

proposal.diagnosis: r91 preserved standing but not heading stability or sustained alternation: settled walking fell at 14.08 s, and direct walking developed yaw 0.416 rad before its first stop and fell at 9.96 s. Reduce the airborne knee reinforcement introduced in r90 while retaining r91's ankle yaw terms and every other coefficient.

plan.hypothesis: Reducing own-foot contact-gated knee reinforcement from 0.060 to 0.055 may improve timely landing and weight acceptance, limiting accumulated turning under the ankle yaw compensation. This tests whether that compensation can coexist with the smaller reinforcement; reduced clearance remains a risk. Paired contributions cancel at zero command.
plan.readout: Compare against r91 for the reinforcement effect and r89 for the ankle-compensation effect. Measure bilateral clearance, flight duration, landing knee extension, support loads, post-landing velocity, yaw growth and foot slip. Require recurring upright alternating support exchanges through initiation, restart and stopping. Report individual walking-segment speeds against 0.50 m/s; exclude falling acceleration from evidence of improvement. Reject same-side-only qualifications, clearance loss, delayed acceptance or growing heading error. Verify standing height, drift and foot separation.

proposal.diagnosis: Reducing airborne knee reinforcement did not resolve r91's instability. r92 retained standing but developed substantial heading drift and fell in both walking trials. Restart alternations occurred during collapse. Attenuate ankle yaw compensation; retain every other r92 coefficient.

plan.hypothesis: Reducing ankle yaw compensation to one-third strength may recover the heading stability lost relative to r89 while retaining some correction of heading-induced ankle imbalance. The geometric correction may be removing useful stabilizing feedback rather than merely correcting coordinates.
plan.readout: Compare yaw growth and lateral drift before failure against r92 and the zero-compensation r89 observations. Measure bilateral ankle clipping, foot slip, clearance, landing placement and post-landing velocity. Require sustained upright alternating support acceptance through onset, restart and stopping, not merely longer survival or collapse-associated footfalls. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s. Check standing drift, height and foot separation because this edit remains active at zero command.

proposal.diagnosis: r93 preserved standing and initial direct walking, but settled walking developed turning/lateral collapse and restart produced planted-foot forward runaway. Neither tested compensation magnitude restored reliable walking. Test the opposite ankle-yaw sign while retaining all other r93 weights.

plan.hypothesis: The heading-dependent ankle imbalance may provide useful stabilizing feedback. Modest reinforcement rather than geometric cancellation could restrain heading drift and preserve support exchange. It could instead amplify asymmetric ankle clipping or overreach; restart failure at small yaw also indicates heading is not the only limitation.
plan.readout: Compare heading growth, lateral drift, ankle imbalance and clipping against r93, using r89's zero-compensation results as prior evidence. Measure bilateral clearance, flight duration, planted-foot slip and post-landing forward velocity. Require recurring upright alternating support acceptance through settled onset and restart, plus stable stopping. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s; reject falling acceleration, same-side-only stepping or survival without useful exchanges. Verify standing height, drift and foot separation.

proposal.diagnosis: r94 completed all three trials upright, including stopping and restart. Walking remained approximately 0.17–0.18 m/s with sparse qualified alternation; settled walking had no qualified touchdowns after 7.86 s. Retain its ankle-yaw feedback and test modestly stronger reciprocal hip motion.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing hip-pitch reciprocal contrast from 0.120 to 0.130 while preserving the common sum of 0.040 may improve swing advance and opposite-leg progression without increasing ankle drive. It could instead cause forward overreach and braking. Paired cancellation preserves zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare bilateral foot advance, clearance, flight duration, touchdown-relative X and post-landing pelvis velocity against r94. Require more frequent consecutive upright alternating support exchanges, including late settled walking and restart. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s. Reject increased reach without weight acceptance, backward deceleration, sliding, ankle saturation or growing heading drift. Verify standing and both stops.

proposal.diagnosis: r95's stronger hip contrast produced no qualified left touchdowns in either walking trial, no speed improvement, and backward restart failure at 12.64 s. Test lower contrast than r94 rather than restoring it; retain all other r95 weights.

plan.hypothesis: Reducing hip-pitch reciprocal contrast from 0.130 to 0.110, with common sum unchanged at 0.040, may reduce premature forward placement and braking while allowing knee-driven clearance and support transfer. It could instead shorten useful steps or cause trailing-foot failure. Zero-command contributions remain cancelled.
plan.readout: Compare against r95 and r94 for bilateral clearance, flight duration, touchdown-relative X, opposite-foot loading and post-landing velocity. Require recurring upright alternating support acceptance, especially left-foot recovery and restart, not shorter shuffling steps alone. Report each walking segment's speed against 0.50 m/s. Reject overreach, trailing-foot runaway, sliding, worsening heading/lateral drift or ankle clipping. Verify standing and stopping.

proposal.diagnosis: r96 preserved standing but both walking trials ended in backward falls. Neither increasing nor decreasing reciprocal hip contrast improved reliably on r94. Test common hip-pitch placement instead, retaining r96's contrast and all unlisted weights.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing the common hip-pitch coefficient sum from 0.040 to 0.050 while keeping reciprocal contrast at 0.110 may shift walking foot placement rearward and reduce braking before backward collapse. plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r157. Examine lateral velocity, selector differences, bilateral loads and contact edges during onset and restart to determine whether shortening follows transfer toward the supporting foot. Favor recurring accepted bilateral steps before sagittal support offsets grow, with bounded lateral motion and stable stops. Oppose amplified rocking, one-sided unloading, premature recontact or either collapse direction. Report within-segment alternation, all-flight clearance and duration, speed versus 0.50 m/s, clipping, slip, heading and pelvis height; exclude collapse-associated qualifications.

proposal.diagnosis: r158 strongly rejects the tested lateral-velocity coupling: seed273 reversed forward velocity by 0.50 s and fell at 1.28 s; previously surviving seed272 also fell backward. Seed271's planted-foot failure remained essentially unchanged. Reverse these selector terms at half magnitude to test whether opposing, rather than reinforcing, velocity-associated phase selection improves coordination. At lateral speed 0.05 m/s, the new argument shift is only 0.025. Retain every other r158 coefficient; matched hidden pairs preserve zero-command cancellation.

plan.hypothesis: Opposite-sign, weaker lateral-velocity coupling may restrain the phase excursions and forward foot drift induced by r158 while preserving useful unloading. It may instead suppress support exchange or destabilize a different phase; the beneficial sign is not established.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r158 and the zero-coupling r157 evidence. Inspect selector differences, lateral velocity, loads and foot placement before any sagittal divergence, especially seed273's first second. Favor bounded placement followed by recurring accepted bilateral steps and stable stops. Reject merely recovering survival without useful exchange, or suppressing motion into double support. Report within-segment alternation, speed versus 0.50 m/s, all-flight clearance and duration, clipping, slip, heading and pelvis height; exclude collapse-associated qualifications.

proposal.diagnosis: r159 recovered seed272 survival and seed273 restart and stopping, unlike r158. However, exchanges remain sparse near 0.20 m/s, and seed271 still falls forward without useful release. Seed273's reported longest alternating run also spans the stop. Increase the retained-sign lateral-velocity selector gain from magnitude 0.50 to 0.75 to test whether its coordination benefit extends beyond recovery of survival. At lateral speed 0.05 m/s, this adds only 0.0125 to each selector argument relative to r159. Retain every other coefficient; zero-command cancellation remains exact.

plan.hypothesis: Moderately stronger lateral-velocity influence in the r159 direction may improve timely support transfer and bilateral swing completion. It may instead overdamp unloading, reinforce side preference or destabilize established walking; seed271 improvement is not implied by the other seeds' recovery.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r159. Require earlier useful release in seed271 and recurring accepted alternation separately within each walking segment in seeds272/273. Examine selector differences against lateral velocity and load transfer to distinguish improved timing from suppression of motion. Report all-flight clearance and duration, walking speeds versus 0.50 m/s, foot-X offsets, clipping, slip, heading, height and stop convergence. Exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated alternation; unchanged seed271 failure would limit the hypothesis's scope.

proposal.diagnosis: r160 improved seed272 to six qualified landings per foot and retained seed273 restart, but seed271 still remained planted until forward collapse. Further lateral-velocity tuning has not solved its initiation. Retain that feedback and introduce a small left-favoring selector offset. At command 0.50 with otherwise neutral selector inputs, this creates approximately 0.057 rad of left-minus-right knee-target difference and 0.013 rad of common hip-roll shift, with little common knee change. This tests whether insufficient initial phase asymmetry traps settled support. The bias persists during walking and could worsen side preference. Matching commanded/uncommanded biases preserves exact zero-command cancellation.

plan.hypothesis: A small coordinated selector asymmetry will initiate unilateral unloading from near-balanced double support, after which measured roll, lateral velocity and foot separation can drive reciprocal exchange. It may instead produce persistent unilateral stepping or disrupt the recovered walking conditions.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r160. In seed271, require useful release and supportive replanting before growing trailing-foot offsets—not merely a longer fall delay. In seeds272/273, check whether both sides continue qualifying and whether repeated same-side steps or heading drift increase. Report selector differences, load transfer, all-flight clearance and duration, within-segment alternation, speed versus 0.50 m/s, clipping, slip, height and stopping convergence. Exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r161's left-favoring offset changed seed271's initial releasing foot but not its 0.04-second flight or subsequent planted-foot collapse. It also eliminated seed272's sustained exchanges and destabilized seed273's restart. Thus selecting a different first foot was insufficient, and the persistent bias was harmful. Test a right-favoring offset at half magnitude rather than restoring r160: left-pair biases become -2.025 and right-pair biases -1.975. Retain every other r161 coefficient. Matching biases within each pair preserves exact zero-command cancellation.

plan.hypothesis: A smaller opposite selector offset may avoid suppressing the established stepping dynamics while testing whether initiation depends on bias direction. It may still merely change the first contact edge without enabling supportive swing completion.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r161 and the unbiased r160 evidence. Distinguish first-foot selection from useful flight, supportive landing and recurring bilateral exchange. In seed271, require support replacement before trailing-foot offsets grow; in seeds272/273, require recovery of accepted within-segment alternation and stable stops. Report speed versus 0.50 m/s, load transfer, all-flight clearance and duration, clipping, slip, heading and height. Exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated alternation; unchanged failure despite reversed first-foot selection would argue against fixed selector bias as the solution.

proposal.diagnosis: r162 recovered seed273 but left seed272 with twelve right-only qualifications and increased lateral drift. Seed271's only qualification occurred after uprightness was lost. Neither selector-bias direction solved initiation. Remove the directional offset by matching the left pair to the retained right-pair bias of -1.975. This does not restore r160: the common selector bias is now slightly more activating than its -2.0. At neutral selector state and command 0.50, paired activation rises from approximately 0.964 to 0.987. Retain every other r162 coefficient; zero-command cancellation remains exact.

plan.hypothesis: Symmetric selectors with slightly increased common activation may recover bilateral exchange without the persistent side preference introduced by unequal biases. The small activation increase may also improve initial unloading, but could instead produce bilateral crouching or disrupt landing acceptance.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r162 and distinguish recovery of bilateral stepping from increased total touchdown count. Require useful support replacement before seed271's trailing-foot divergence, recurring within-segment alternation in seeds272/273, and stable stops. Inspect bilateral selector activation, knee targets, load transfer, all-flight clearance and duration, pelvis height, heading and lateral drift. Report walking speeds versus 0.50 m/s, clipping and slip; exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated qualifications. If seed271 remains unchanged, do not credit restored performance elsewhere as robust initiation.

proposal.diagnosis: r163 recovered bilateral qualifications in seed272 but retained right-side dominance and roughly 0.20 m/s walking. Seed271 still replanted after a 0.04-second release and fell forward without useful support replacement. Selector-bias changes have not solved this initiation failure.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing selector-driven lateral hip action by 12.5%, while retaining r163 selection and knee commands, may produce sufficient load transfer for sustained unilateral release. It could instead amplify lateral rocking or disrupt landing acceptance. Paired cancellation preserves the zero-command policy.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r163. Inspect selector differences, hip-roll targets and actual angles, lateral velocity and bilateral loads at 0.02-second resolution during onset and restart. Test whether stronger lateral action produces unloading followed by supportive landing before sagittal offsets diverge, especially in seed271. Report within-segment accepted alternation, all-flight clearance and duration, walking speed versus 0.50 m/s, height, heading, slip, clipping and stop convergence. Reject delayed falls, stationary double support, excessive rocking and collapse-associated or cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r164 did not resolve seed271's immediate recontact and planted-foot collapse. Seeds272/273 survived, but seed273's restart qualified only left-foot landings. Stronger lateral action therefore did not establish reliable bilateral swing completion.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing contact-gated knee flexion may sustain an initially released foot long enough for useful advancement instead of immediate recontact. Retain all other r164 weights. Earlier evidence that weaker reinforcement improved restart makes delayed extension and poor landing acceptance explicit risks. Zero-command contributions still cancel.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r164. Inspect knee targets, actual flexion, clearance, foot advancement and supporting-foot load around every release and recontact, especially seed271's first 0.04-second flight. Require subsequent supportive landings and recurring bilateral exchange, not longer flight alone. Report within-segment alternation, walking speed versus 0.50 m/s, foot-X offsets, height, clipping, slip, heading and stopping convergence. Check whether increased airborne flexion delays load acceptance or causes backward deterioration. Exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated qualifications.

proposal.diagnosis: r165 produced simultaneous 0.04-second foot releases in seed271, followed by the same planted-foot collapse. Increased airborne reinforcement did not establish support exchange. Other seeds survived near 0.20 m/s, but bilateral qualifications remained inconsistent.

plan.hypothesis: Reducing common selector-driven knee flexion while preserving its left-right contrast may maintain supporting-leg extension during initiation rather than briefly unloading both feet. Retain r165's airborne reinforcement. This could instead suppress clearance or produce excessively stiff landings; zero-command cancellation remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r165. Verify that the knee coefficient sum decreases from 0.214 to 0.194 while contrast remains 0.534. Inspect knee targets and angles, pelvis vertical motion, simultaneous flight, supporting-foot loads and recontact timing during onset and restart. Require useful unilateral release followed by supportive landing before seed271's trailing-foot offsets grow. Report recurring within-segment bilateral alternation, all-flight clearance and duration, speed versus 0.50 m/s, height, clipping, slip, heading and stopping convergence. Reject stationary double support, delayed collapse and cross-stop or collapse-associated qualifications.

proposal.diagnosis: r166 eliminated seed271's brief initial release without preventing its forward collapse, and seed273 lost restart stability. Reduced common knee flexion alone did not improve support exchange. Surviving walking remained near 0.20 m/s with predominantly right-foot qualifications in seed272.

plan.hypothesis: Increasing selector-driven knee contrast from 0.534 to 0.574 while retaining the reduced common sum of 0.194 may separate swing shortening from support extension enough to restore useful unilateral release. It may instead amplify rocking or compromise landing acceptance. All other r166 coefficients remain unchanged; zero-command cancellation is preserved.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r166. Inspect selector differences, bilateral knee targets and angles, loads and contact edges during onset and restart. Determine whether increased contrast creates supported unilateral flight before foot-X offsets diverge, rather than simultaneous unloading or ineffective joint motion under load. Require recurring accepted bilateral landings within each walking segment and stable stops. Report all-flight clearance and duration, walking speed versus 0.50 m/s, height, heading, slip and clipping. Exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated alternation; delayed falls alone are not improvement.

proposal.diagnosis: r167 left seed271's planted-foot failure unchanged and introduced backward collapse in seed272. Seed273 was already slowing and turning before its stop, then fell. Greater knee contrast did not yield reliable support replacement.

plan.hypothesis: With r167's knee contrast retained, reducing selector-driven hip-pitch contrast from 0.14 to 0.12 while preserving its common sum of 0.05 may limit excessive swing reach and landing braking. It could instead shorten advancement and worsen planted-foot failure. Zero-command cancellation remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r167. Inspect hip targets and angles, foot-X offsets at touchdown, supporting-leg motion and post-touchdown velocity before deterioration. Test whether reduced hip excursion bounds placement without sacrificing clearance or support replacement. Require recurring accepted bilateral landings separately within each walking segment and stable stops. Report speed versus 0.50 m/s, all-flight clearance and duration, loads, height, heading, clipping and slip. Explicitly retain seed271 as an initiation test; reject mere fall delay, stationary support, cross-stop alternation and collapse-associated qualifications.

proposal.diagnosis: Reducing hip excursion in r168 accelerated backward deterioration in seeds272/273 and left seed271's planted-foot collapse unchanged. Longer flights and greater clearance did not translate into sustained support. The increased knee contrast remains a plausible contributor to poor landing acceptance.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce knee contrast from 0.574 to 0.534 while preserving its common sum of 0.194 and retaining r168's reduced hip excursion. This tests whether excessive knee differentiation, rather than hip reach alone, drives the backward deterioration. It may recover supportive landings but further suppress useful release.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r168; use r166 as the complementary comparison with identical knee coefficients but larger hip excursion. Inspect knee extension, touchdown loads, foot-X offsets and post-landing velocity before deterioration. Require recurring accepted bilateral steps within each walking segment, bounded placement and stable stops—not merely later falls or greater clearance. Report speed versus 0.50 m/s, all-flight duration and clearance, height, heading, slip and clipping. Keep seed271's lack of release explicit and exclude cross-stop or collapse-associated alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r169 delayed backward collapse but did not recover sustained walking. Seed273 was already slowing and leaning backward before stopping; seed271 still failed without useful release. Reducing knee contrast alone was insufficient.

plan.hypothesis: Increase common selector-driven hip extension from a coefficient sum of 0.05 to 0.07 while preserving hip contrast at 0.12. This may reduce accumulating anterior foot placement without further reducing swing excursion. It could instead worsen seed271's trailing-foot failure. Retain all other r169 weights; zero-command cancellation remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r169. Inspect hip targets and actual angles, touchdown foot-X offsets, support loads and post-landing velocity before backward deterioration. Require bounded placement and recurring accepted bilateral landings within each walking segment, not merely delayed collapse. For seed271, check whether useful release occurs before the pelvis overruns planted feet. Report speed versus 0.50 m/s, all-flight clearance and duration, height, heading, slip, clipping and stop convergence. Exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r170's added common hip extension did not prevent backward deterioration; seed273 slowed and turned substantially before stopping. Seed271's planted-foot failure remained unchanged. Reduced reciprocal hip excursion remains suspect rather than established as beneficial.

plan.hypothesis: Increase hip-pitch contrast from 0.12 to 0.14 while retaining the common sum of 0.07 and all other r170 coefficients. Stronger reciprocal hip motion may improve support replacement and prevent accumulating placement errors. It could instead increase overreach or landing braking. Zero-command cancellation remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r170. Inspect swing advancement, stance-leg motion, touchdown foot-X offsets, loads and post-touchdown velocity before deterioration. Distinguish improved reciprocal support replacement from simply larger foot excursions. Require recurring accepted bilateral landings within each walking segment, bounded heading and placement, and stable stops. Report speed versus 0.50 m/s, all-flight clearance and duration, height, clipping and slip. Seed271 must achieve useful release before trailing-foot divergence; exclude delayed collapse, cross-stop alternation and collapse-associated qualifications.

proposal.diagnosis: r171 recovered survival and stopping in seeds272/273, but walking remained near 0.20 m/s with strongly right-dominated qualifications. Seed271 still never released usefully. Survival recovery does not establish reliable alternation or target-speed tracking.

plan.hypothesis: Increase ankle command drive after forward motion develops while approximately preserving its contribution at target 0.50 m/s and zero actual velocity through compensating h8/h9 weights. This tests whether stronger progression improves speed and support exchange without a larger initial drive jump. Earlier compensated-drive experiments showed a risk of planted-foot runaway. Zero-command behavior remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r171. Verify near-zero initial ankle-command difference, then inspect how the change develops with forward velocity. Report walking-segment speed and tracking error versus 0.50 m/s alongside accepted bilateral alternation, touchdown loads, foot-X offsets, slip and ankle clipping. Require sustained supported progression rather than faster sliding or falling. Inspect seed271 onset and seed273 restart for divergence before useful release; also report clearance, flight duration, height, heading and stopping convergence. Exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated qualifications.

proposal.diagnosis: r172 modestly increased surviving walking speed and improved seed273's bilateral qualifications, but seed272 qualified only right-foot landings. Seed271 fell sooner without releasing either foot before collapse. Stronger progression has not solved initiation from balanced support.

plan.hypothesis: Add a small low-speed, command-gated lateral hip shift using h8-h9. Unlike amplifying a nearly balanced selector, this provides an initiating weight shift that diminishes as forward speed develops. It may enable unilateral unloading before sagittal runaway, but could instead enforce side preference or destabilize restart. All other r172 weights remain unchanged; the added terms cancel at zero command.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r172. During onset and restart, inspect h8-h9, lateral hip targets and angles, pelvis lateral motion, bilateral loads and contact edges. Require supported unilateral release followed by useful replanting before trailing-foot offsets grow. Check whether the added shift diminishes during progression and permits recurring bilateral exchange rather than persistent one-sided stepping. Report within-segment alternation, speed versus 0.50 m/s, all-flight clearance and duration, height, heading, slip, clipping and stop convergence. Exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated qualifications; delayed falls alone are insufficient.

proposal.diagnosis: r173 did not release seed271's planted feet and introduced forward-collapse failures in seed272 and seed273's restart. Initial walking in seed273 survived, so the added shift appears particularly harmful during settled initiation; its direction versus its presence remains unresolved.

plan.hypothesis: Reverse the low-speed lateral shift at unchanged magnitude, retaining every other r173 coefficient. This tests whether initiation requires the opposite load-transfer direction rather than stronger lateral action. The reversed shift may instead reproduce planted-foot failure or impose the opposite side preference. Added contributions still cancel at zero command.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r173 and the unshifted r172 evidence. Inspect onset and restart at 0.02-second resolution: lateral hip targets, actual angles, bilateral loads, selector differences, contact edges and foot-X offsets. Require supported unilateral release followed by load-bearing replanting before sagittal divergence. Report accepted alternation separately within each walking segment, speed error versus 0.50 m/s, clearance, flight duration, slip, ankle clipping, height, heading and stop convergence. Do not credit changed first-foot selection, delayed collapse or cross-stop alternation as sustained walking.

proposal.diagnosis: Reversing the shift restored seed272 survival but left seed271's initiation failure unchanged. Seed273 became left-only and fell backward after restart, whereas unshifted r172 survived both walking segments. Neither tested shift direction established robust initiation.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce the negative lateral-shift magnitude by 75%, retaining all other r174 weights. A weaker shift may preserve seed272's recovery without disrupting seed273's bilateral exchange and restart. This tests amplitude sensitivity, not an assumed cure for seed271. Zero-command cancellation remains exact.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r174 and unshifted r172. Measure onset and restart load asymmetry, lateral motion, first supported release, touchdown load acceptance and foot-X divergence. Determine whether reduced shift restores recurring bilateral landings rather than merely changing the preferred foot. Report walking-segment mean speed and error versus 0.50 m/s, within-segment alternating runs, clearance, flight duration, slip, clipping, height, heading and stop convergence. Keep seed271's initiation failure explicit; exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r175 recovered seed273's restart survival, but seed272 remained right-only and seed271 again fell without useful release. Lateral-shift tuning has not corrected initiation. Successful progression remains approximately 0.21 m/s, far below the command.

plan.hypothesis: Increase low-speed ankle compensation by 0.03 without changing the direct command coefficient or any other r175 weight. At command 0.50 and zero velocity, this raises each ankle target by approximately 0.029; the change diminishes with forward speed. This tests whether a smaller initial sagittal drive allows support exchange before planted-foot runaway. It could instead suppress progression or induce backward deterioration. Zero-command behavior remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r175. Inspect ankle targets before clipping, actual ankle angles, pitch, velocity, foot-X offsets and bilateral loads during onset and restart. Require useful release and load-bearing replanting before sagittal divergence, not merely slower collapse. Report within-segment accepted bilateral alternation, walking speed and error versus 0.50 m/s, flight duration, clearance, slip, clipping, height, heading and stop convergence. Distinguish stable double support from walking; exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated qualifications.

proposal.diagnosis: r176 delayed seed271's fall by only 0.08 seconds without useful release. Seeds272/273 retained survival and stable stops, but bilateral exchange remained sparse at approximately 0.21 m/s. Smaller initial ankle drive did not resolve the planted-foot initiation mode.

plan.hypothesis: Add modest opposing low-speed knee contributions: left flexion and right extension. At command 0.50 and zero velocity, these change normalized knee targets by approximately +0.024 and -0.024, preserving their mean. This tests direct leg-length differentiation when the existing selectors remain nearly balanced. Earlier stronger gated knee asymmetry failed, so excessive side preference and poor landing acceptance remain explicit risks. Retain every other r176 coefficient; zero-command contributions cancel.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r176. During onset and restart, inspect bilateral knee targets and actual angles, supporting-foot load, pelvis height and the first release/replant sequence. Require supportive unilateral flight before trailing-foot divergence, followed by recurring bilateral exchange as the added contribution diminishes with forward speed. Report walking-segment speed error versus 0.50 m/s, within-segment alternating runs, clearance, flight duration, foot-X offsets, slip, clipping, heading and stop convergence. Reject simultaneous unloading, persistent left-only stepping, delayed collapse and cross-stop or collapse-associated qualifications.

proposal.diagnosis: r177 changed seed272's dominant qualified foot from right to left without establishing recurring alternation. Seed271 remained planted until collapse, while seed273 newly fell backward at 2.98 seconds. The knee asymmetry strongly affects stepping but its tested direction was detrimental.

plan.hypothesis: Reverse the low-speed knee asymmetry at unchanged magnitude: right flexion and left extension. Retain every other r177 coefficient. This tests whether the failure depends on which leg is shortened rather than asymmetry alone. It may instead reproduce one-sided stepping or backward deterioration. The knee mean and zero-command cancellation remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r177 and the zero-knee-asymmetry r176 evidence. Inspect initial knee targets and actual angles, bilateral loads, foot release, advancement and load acceptance. In seed273, examine placement and velocity before 2 seconds rather than interpreting collapse-associated clearance as improvement. Require seed271 support replacement before trailing-foot divergence and recurring accepted bilateral exchange elsewhere. Report within-segment alternating runs, speed error versus 0.50 m/s, clearance, flight duration, foot-X offsets, slip, clipping, height, heading and stopping convergence. Changed side preference or delayed falls alone do not support the hypothesis.

proposal.diagnosis: r178 restored seed273 survival but retained right-dominant stepping and substantial lateral drift. Seed271's initial right-foot release lasted only 0.04 seconds before the familiar planted-foot collapse. Reversing knee asymmetry changed side preference, not sustained support replacement.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce common sagittal foot-position feedback into both ankles by 10%, from a coefficient sum of -10 to -9, preserving the own-versus-other contrast of -6. Retain all other r178 weights. This tests whether strong common feedback amplifies placement errors and ankle saturation before support replacement. Saturation may instead be a consequence of failed stepping; weaker feedback could impair standing, which requires a dedicated check.
plan.readout: Compare seed271 onset and seed273's full profile with r178. Inspect common foot-X displacement, individual ankle feedback contributions before clipping, actual ankle angles, pitch and velocity before divergence. Require supported release, load-bearing replanting and recurring within-segment bilateral exchange—not simply reduced clipping or delayed falls. Report walking speed error versus 0.50 m/s, clearance, flight duration, slip, heading and lateral drift. In the standing trial, track height, pitch, velocity, stance width and displacement throughout 20 seconds. Exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r179 preserved standalone standing but accelerated seed271's collapse and introduced seed273's final-stop failure. Reducing common ankle foot-position feedback did not improve support replacement. It also changed the posture reached before walking, so the effect cannot be attributed solely to walking-phase feedback.

plan.hypothesis: Test stronger common ankle foot-position feedback: coefficient sum -10.5, with own-versus-other contrast still -6. Retain every other r179 weight. This brackets the unsuccessful -9 setting against the earlier -10 evidence and tests whether stronger sagittal stabilization bounds placement during walking and stopping. It may instead increase saturation or destabilize standing.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r179 and r178. Record posture, foot-X offsets and ankle targets immediately before command transitions to distinguish standing-state changes from subsequent dynamics. Inspect feedback contributions before clipping, pitch, velocity, supporting-foot loads and replanting. Require sustained support replacement and recurring within-segment bilateral steps, not merely later falls. Report speed error versus 0.50 m/s, clearance, flight duration, slip, clipping, heading and lateral drift. Check the full standing trial for convergence, height loss and stance widening; exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r180 retained standing and restored seed273's stop survival, but its sole reported alternation crossed the stop: the first walking segment qualified only left landings and the restart only right landings. Seed271 still collapsed without useful support replacement. Stronger ankle feedback delayed that failure rather than resolving it.

plan.hypothesis: Remove only the fixed-side, low-speed knee asymmetry while retaining r180's stronger ankle feedback and every other coefficient. The asymmetry failed to establish useful initiation and may bias subsequent support exchange. Removing it may recover bilateral stepping with the new ankle setting, but could suppress the brief initial release. The zero-command policy remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare with r180, and use r176 as contextual evidence with zero knee asymmetry but weaker common ankle feedback. Count accepted alternation separately within each walking segment; explicitly discard seed273's cross-stop side switch. Inspect knee targets, bilateral loads, clearance, flight duration, touchdown placement and load acceptance. Require seed271 replanting before trailing-foot divergence and recurring bilateral exchange elsewhere. Report walking speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, heading, lateral drift and stop convergence; survival or later collapse alone is insufficient.

proposal.diagnosis: Removing knee asymmetry preserved survival in seeds272/273 and improved some bilateral exchange, but seed273's first walking segment remained left-only. Seed271 still failed without release. Earlier r163–r164 evidence suggests increasing lateral selector action from 0.32 to 0.36 impaired bilateral stepping.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce selector-driven lateral hip action from 0.36 to 0.32 while retaining every other r181 coefficient, including stronger ankle feedback. Smaller lateral excursions may improve transfer timing and landing acceptance rather than repeatedly shortening one foot's flight. It could instead weaken unloading. This revisits an individually supported coefficient change under the current weights; zero-command behavior remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r181. Inspect selector differences, hip-roll targets and actual angles, lateral velocity, bilateral loads and release-to-replant timing. Measure both short unqualified flights and accepted landings to distinguish improved exchange from qualification-threshold effects. Require recurring bilateral support replacement within each walking segment; exclude seed273's cross-stop side switch. Report speed error versus 0.50 m/s, clearance, flight duration, slip, clipping, height, heading, drift and stopping convergence. Keep seed271's initiation failure separate from improvements elsewhere; delayed collapse is not success.

proposal.diagnosis: r182 improved accepted bilateral exchange in seeds272/273 while preserving stops, supporting a smaller lateral selector gain. However, stepping remains irregular near 0.22 m/s, seed272's drift increased, and seed271 still failed without useful release.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce lateral selector gain another 6.25%, from 0.32 to 0.30, retaining every other r182 coefficient. This tests whether the improvement continues toward more consistent support exchange or whether unloading becomes too weak. Zero-command behavior remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r182. Measure lateral excursion, bilateral load-transfer timing, all release durations and load-bearing landings—not just qualified touchdown counts. Require recurring alternation within each walking segment, without increased slip or lateral drift. Report walking speed error versus 0.50 m/s, clearance, flight duration, foot-X offsets, clipping, height, heading and stop convergence. Treat seed271 initiation separately: improvement requires support replacement before planted-foot divergence. Exclude cross-stop alternation and collapse-associated contacts.

proposal.diagnosis: Reducing lateral selector gain to 0.30 did not continue r182's improvement: seed273's restart had only left qualified landings, and alternating runs shortened in both surviving trials. Speed remains near 0.21 m/s; seed271 still falls without useful release.

plan.hypothesis: Set lateral selector gain to 0.33, retaining every other r183 coefficient. Testing just above 0.32 distinguishes a narrow favorable transfer-timing region from the unsupported assumption that progressively smaller lateral action improves walking. Zero-command behavior remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r183 and r182. Record all foot-off durations, clearance, bilateral loads, lateral excursion and load acceptance after touchdown, including unqualified flights. Require recurring bilateral support replacement within each walking segment, not merely more threshold-qualified contacts. Report segment speed and error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, foot-X offsets, clipping, height, heading, drift and stop convergence. Analyze seed271 initiation separately; delayed collapse is not improvement. Exclude cross-stop and collapse-associated alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: Lateral-gain tuning has not resolved initiation: seed271 still falls without support replacement. At 0.33, seed273 also falls backward on restart. Surviving progression remains near 0.21 m/s with irregular bilateral landings.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce own-foot contact-gated knee flexion from 0.0675 to 0.0575, retaining every other r184 coefficient. Earlier development supported this reduction in a different configuration. Less airborne flexion may improve timely extension and landing acceptance, but could instead reduce clearance and shorten already marginal flights. Zero-command behavior remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r184. Inspect contact-gate contributions, knee targets and angles, all flight durations, clearance, touchdown placement and subsequent load acceptance. For seed273, capture restart through the first velocity reversal to distinguish failed placement from failed support. Require recurring bilateral exchange within each walking segment; fewer qualified contacts could reflect inadequate clearance rather than better landing. Report speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, heading, drift and stopping convergence. Seed271 must replace support before trailing-foot divergence; delayed falls and cross-stop alternation do not count.

proposal.diagnosis: Reduced contact-gated flexion decreased qualified landings without resolving either failure: seed271 remained planted until collapse, and seed273 fell backward on restart. Lower flexion has not demonstrated better support acceptance.

plan.hypothesis: Increase own-foot contact-gated knee flexion to 0.0725, retaining every other r185 coefficient. This tests slightly above r184's 0.0675 setting whether insufficient clearance and premature recontact limit bilateral exchange. Excessive flexion could instead delay extension and worsen landing support. Zero-command behavior remains unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r185 and r184. Measure every flight's clearance, duration and advancement, followed by touchdown load acceptance and velocity change. Distinguish genuine support replacement from contacts merely crossing qualification thresholds. Inspect seed273's restart before velocity reversal; require seed271 release and replanting before foot-X divergence. Report within-segment bilateral alternating runs, speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, heading, lateral drift and stop convergence. Exclude cross-stop alternation and collapse-associated contacts.

proposal.diagnosis: r186 restored seed273's restart survival and bilateral landings, but seed272 remains right-dominant and seed271 still never releases usefully. Progression remains near 0.21 m/s. Clearance tuning alone has not resolved support-transfer timing.

plan.hypothesis: Increase mirrored lateral-velocity input to the selectors from magnitude 0.75 to 1.00, retaining every other r186 coefficient. Earlier increases in this direction supported exchange. Greater velocity sensitivity may improve phase switching before lateral transfer reverses, but could instead suppress unloading or cause premature switching. Matched hidden pairs preserve exact zero-command cancellation.
plan.readout: Compare identical profiles with r186. Record selector differences against lateral velocity, roll, bilateral loads and contact edges, including their effects on knee, hip and ankle targets. Determine whether switching produces supported release and load-bearing replanting rather than contact chatter. Require recurring bilateral exchange separately within each walking segment. plan.hypothesis: Increase selector lateral-velocity sensitivity from magnitude 1.25 to 1.50, retaining every other r294 coefficient.
