The earlier reduction at r288 reduced alternation in settled starts, but that does not guarantee improvement here. Premature phase reversal and increased lateral excursion are risks. Matched hidden pairs preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r294. Decompose selector contributions and align phase reversals with lateral velocity, roll, bilateral loads, releases and recontacts. Inspect the first three commanded seconds and the interval preceding deceleration. Measure all flights' duration, clearance and advancement; require landing load acceptance followed by opposite-foot release. Report within-segment alternating runs, landing gaps, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Evaluate stopping convergence and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r295 restored both settled-start trials to full survival, but walking remained near 0.20 m/s with sparse alternation. Seed273 produced no qualified landings and fell forward after deceleration and placement asymmetry. Its falling acceleration is not speed-tracking progress.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce own-foot contact-gated knee flexion from 0.110 to 0.105, retaining every other r295 coefficient. Test whether less airborne shortening improves timely load acceptance while retaining the increased hip advancement. Earlier increases above 0.105 disrupted direct-start walking in another configuration. Reduced clearance and premature recontact are risks; improvement is not guaranteed. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r295. Align contact-gated knee contributions, actual knee extension, foot advancement, clearance, recontact and landing loads. Inspect seed273's first three seconds and determine whether landings accept support and permit opposite-foot release before deceleration. Record qualified and unqualified flights, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Evaluate stopping convergence and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: Reduced knee shortening did not recover reciprocal walking: seed271 lost survival, seed273 remained left-only, and seed272 survived near 0.20 m/s. Seed271's 9.10 s touchdown occurred during collapse. Seed273's backward divergence preceded the stop command.

plan.hypothesis: Increase speed-gate velocity sensitivity from −5.0 to −5.5, retaining every other r296 coefficient. Test whether reducing positive ankle compensation during forward motion improves progression and support replacement. The earlier broadening to −5.0 suppressed qualified landings in another configuration. Initial compensation at zero velocity and all zero-command outputs remain unchanged. The gate also affects hip pitch and roll; increased negative ankle saturation and backward instability are risks.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r296. Decompose h8−h9 contributions and align ankle targets, clipping, actual ankle motion, velocity, pitch and foot placement before divergence. Determine whether improved progression accompanies load-bearing advancing landings followed by opposite-foot release, rather than slip or falling acceleration. Measure all flights' duration, clearance and advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, height, roll, heading, drift and stopping convergence. Evaluate initial walking and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r297 restored settled-start survival, but qualified landings remained strongly left-biased and speed stayed near 0.20 m/s. Seed273 accumulated positive lateral drift and unequal foot placement before stopping; its later fall cannot be attributed solely to the stop command.

plan.hypothesis: Halve the common hip-roll speed-gate offset from magnitude 0.02 to 0.01, retaining every other r297 coefficient. Test whether reducing this directional bias, strongest at low forward velocity, limits startup drift and permits reciprocal support exchange without changing selector timing or ankle compensation. Loss of useful initiation assistance and reversal of the favored side are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r297. Separate speed-gated hip-roll offsets from selector contributions; align actual hip-roll motion, lateral velocity, roll, bilateral loads and foot placement before sagittal deceleration. Require advancing landings that accept load and enable opposite-foot release, not merely reduced drift or a change in favored side. Record all flight durations, clearances, advancements, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch, heading and stopping convergence. Evaluate restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: Halving the hip-roll offset eliminated seed271's initiation while improving seed272's landing balance. Seed273 still developed substantial drift and was already accelerating into a forward fall before stopping. The offset affects initiation as well as directional bias.

plan.hypothesis: Increase common hip-roll speed-gate offset magnitude from 0.010 to 0.015, retaining every other r298 coefficient. Test whether partial restoration recovers seed271's early unloading without losing seed272's bilateral exchanges. Endpoint results demonstrate sensitivity, not a guaranteed stable midpoint. Renewed directional bias and impaired direct-start walking are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r298 and r297. Inspect the first two commanded seconds for load transfer and release before velocity reversal. Separate speed-gated offsets from selector contributions; align actual hip-roll motion, lateral velocity, bilateral loads and foot placement. Measure every flight's duration, clearance, advancement and landing load acceptance, followed by opposite-foot release. Report within-segment alternating runs, landing gaps, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Assess pre-stop posture, stopping convergence and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: The intermediate hip-roll offset did not recover seed271 initiation; its sole qualified landing occurred during collapse. Seed272 remained upright but slow with sparse alternation. Seed273 again developed backward divergence before stopping. Offset interpolation has not resolved support replacement.

plan.hypothesis: Increase selector-driven hip-pitch contrast from 0.175 to 0.185 while preserving the coefficient sum at 0.080. Retain every other r299 coefficient. Test whether stronger reciprocal hip motion improves swing advancement and stance-to-swing separation without increasing common hip-pitch demand or changing selector timing. Overreach, backward instability and disrupted load acceptance are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r299. Separate common and differential hip-pitch contributions; align actual hip angles, bilateral foot advancement, loads, release and recontact. Inspect seed271's first two commanded seconds and seed273 before deceleration. Require advancing landings that accept load and permit opposite-foot release. Measure all flights, clearance, advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Assess pre-stop posture, stopping convergence and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: Increasing hip-pitch contrast restored seed271 survival and retained seed272 survival, but neither achieved sustained alternation or 0.50 m/s. Seed273 still had only one qualified left landing, with drift and sagittal divergence preceding its stop.

plan.hypothesis: Increase selector-driven hip-pitch contrast from 0.185 to 0.195 while preserving the coefficient sum at 0.080. Retain every other r300 coefficient. Test whether additional reciprocal excursion improves support replacement beyond the initiation benefit observed at r300. This is not an assumption of monotonic improvement: overreach, premature landing and backward instability are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r300. Align differential hip targets, actual hip motion, bilateral foot advancement, releases, landing loads and subsequent opposite-foot release. Determine whether the weaker side improves without sacrificing the stronger side. Inspect seed273 before lateral drift and deceleration; distinguish placement failure from insufficient clearance or abbreviated flight. Record all flight durations, clearances, advancements, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Assess stopping and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r301 achieved full survival and stopping across all three profiles, including seed273's restart. However, seeds271/273 had no qualified right landings, and seed272 alternated only once. Walking remained near 0.20–0.22 m/s; survival has not established reciprocal gait.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce opposing hip-pitch speed-gate offsets from magnitude 0.012 to 0.009, retaining every other r301 coefficient, including hip-pitch contrast 0.195. Test whether reducing persistent placement asymmetry permits right-foot advancement while the stronger selector-driven motion preserves initiation. Earlier offset reductions disrupted initiation in other configurations; renewed initiation failure and loss of left-foot advancement are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r301. Separate speed-gated hip offsets from selector contributions and align actual hip angles, bilateral advancement, clearance, release timing and landing loads. Determine whether right advancing landings increase without sacrificing left landings or merely reversing the favored side. Require load acceptance followed by opposite-foot release. Record all flights, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Evaluate initial walking, stopping convergence and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: Reducing hip speed-gate asymmetry at r302 produced bilateral landings during seed273's initial walking, but all three trials ultimately fell, versus full survival at r301. Seed271's late right touchdown does not establish healthy alternation. Walking speed remains approximately 0.20–0.22 m/s.

plan.hypothesis: Increase opposing hip-pitch speed-gate offset magnitude from 0.009 to 0.0105, retaining every other r302 coefficient. Test whether partial restoration preserves initiation and stopping robustness while retaining bilateral placement. Endpoint results indicate sensitivity, not a guaranteed stable midpoint. Renewed unilateral stepping is a risk. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r302 and r301. Separate speed-gated offsets from selector contributions; align actual hip motion, heading drift, foot advancement, landing loads and subsequent opposite-foot release before deceleration. Record all flight durations, clearance, advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright walking speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch and roll. Evaluate stopping convergence and restart separately, including residual heading and stance asymmetry. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r303 recovered both settled-start trials, but neither produced qualified alternation. Seed273 achieved an initial exchange, stopped upright, then fell backward after restart. Frequent brief releases suggest investigating swing clearance and duration rather than further tuning the hip asymmetry.

plan.hypothesis: Increase own-foot contact-gated knee flexion from 0.105 to 0.110, retaining every other r303 coefficient. Test whether slightly greater airborne shortening converts brief releases into advancing, load-bearing landings with reciprocal support exchange. The earlier reduction at r296 impaired settled-start survival, although that configuration differed. Excessive shortening, delayed load acceptance and restart instability are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r303. Measure every flight, including unqualified releases: duration, clearance, advancement, actual knee motion, landing load acceptance and delay to opposite-foot release. Separate inadequate clearance from premature selector reversal. Report within-segment alternating runs, landing gaps, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Inspect seed273's pre-restart stance and first second after restart; assess stopping convergence separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r304 eliminated seed271's early stepping and did not restore seed272 alternation. Seed273 improved to an initial L–R–L sequence but produced no qualified restart landings before falling. Greater airborne knee flexion alone did not resolve support exchange.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce selector roll-rate sensitivity from magnitude 0.065 to 0.060, retaining every other r304 coefficient. Test whether less anticipatory phase switching allows swing advancement and load acceptance before reversal, particularly during initiation and restart. Delayed unloading and excessive lateral excursion are risks. Matched hidden pairs preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r304. Align selector reversals and their roll-rate contributions with foot release, actual hip/knee motion, recontact and bilateral loads. Determine whether longer useful swing precedes load-bearing advancement and opposite-foot release, rather than merely increasing flight duration. Record qualified and unqualified flights, clearance, advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Inspect seed271's first two commanded seconds and seed273's restart separately; assess stopping convergence. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r305 restored seed271 initiation but not sustained alternation; it was physically down despite reaching the horizon. Seed272 retained sparse bilateral landings, while seed273 again fell backward after restart. Upright walking remains near 0.20–0.22 m/s.

plan.hypothesis: Increase speed-gate velocity sensitivity from −5.5 to −6.0, retaining every other r305 coefficient. Test whether reducing positive ankle compensation during forward motion improves progression through support exchange. The −5.0 to −5.5 change at r297 improved settled-start survival in another configuration. Initial compensation at zero velocity and all zero-command outputs remain unchanged. The gate also affects hip pitch and roll; negative ankle saturation, disrupted initiation and backward instability are risks.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r305. Decompose h8−h9 contributions and align unclipped ankle targets, actual ankle motion, velocity, pitch, foot placement and bilateral loads before divergence. Require advancing landings that accept load and enable opposite-foot release, not displacement from slip or falling. Record every flight's duration, clearance and advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, clipping, height, roll, heading and drift. Inspect restart onset and stopping convergence separately. Treat physical collapse as failure regardless of horizon termination; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r306 did not establish sustained alternation. Seed271 fell backward earlier, seed272 remained upright with sparse exchanges, and seed273 again failed after restarting from an upright stop. Increased speed-gate sensitivity alone did not resolve support replacement.

plan.hypothesis: Increase bilateral ankle speed-gate output magnitude by 0.020, retaining every other r306 coefficient. At command 0.50 and zero velocity this raises ankle targets by approximately 0.0193; the increment becomes smaller during forward motion. Test whether modestly relieving negative ankle demand improves initiation and restart without losing moving-state progression. Excess compensation could suppress stepping or induce forward instability. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r306. Align speed-gate contributions, unclipped ankle targets, clipping, actual ankle motion, pitch, velocity and foot placement during the first two seconds of each start. Require load-bearing advancing landings followed by opposite-foot release, not merely longer survival. Record every flight's duration, clearance and advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, height, roll, heading and drift. Assess stopping convergence and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r307 prolonged seed271 walking and enabled seed273 restart advancement, but stepping remained predominantly unilateral. Seed271 was already falling before the stop command. Seed273's reported alternation crossed the stop interval; neither walking segment contained qualified alternation.

plan.hypothesis: Strengthen opposite-foot contact-gated knee extension from magnitude 0.0125 to 0.0175, retaining every other r307 coefficient. At command 0.50, the incremental knee-target reduction is approximately 0.00482 when the opposite foot is airborne versus 0.00018 when planted. Test whether stronger stance support during opposite-foot flight improves swing completion and reciprocal load transfer. Excessive extension, impact loading and disrupted unloading are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r307. Align opposite-foot contact gates, stance-knee motion, pelvis height, bilateral loads, swing clearance and landing timing. Require advancing landings that accept load and permit subsequent opposite-foot release. Record all flights, including unqualified ones, with duration, clearance and advancement; calculate alternation and landing gaps separately within each walking segment. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Evaluate stopping convergence and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r308 restored seed271 survival and seed273 restart survival, but exchanges remained sparse or unilateral; seed272 fell backward. Stronger stance support helped some trajectories without establishing sustained alternating walking.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce selector-driven hip-pitch contrast from 0.195 to 0.190 while preserving its coefficient sum at 0.080. Retain every other r308 coefficient, including strengthened opposite-foot knee support. Test whether slightly less reciprocal excursion improves landing placement and load acceptance without losing initiation. Earlier contrast increases improved survival but reduced alternation in some trials. Insufficient advancement and renewed initiation failure are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r308. Align differential hip targets, actual hip motion, foot placement relative to the pelvis, landing loads and subsequent opposite-foot release. Determine whether shorter excursion reduces braking or premature recontact rather than merely reducing advancement. Record all flights' duration, clearance and advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Inspect seed272 before deceleration and assess stopping and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r309 retained seed271 and seed273 survival and improved seed272's early alternating run, but seed272 still fell backward. Seed271 remained entirely left-qualified; seed273 alternated only late in restart. Support exchange remains a limitation despite adequate advancement on the favored side.

plan.hypothesis: Increase selector-driven hip-roll output magnitude from 0.35 to 0.36, retaining every other r309 coefficient. Test whether stronger lateral load transfer enables the weaker foot to complete useful swings without further increasing sagittal excursion. Excessive lateral motion, premature unloading and loss of landing support are risks. Matched output pairs preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r309. Align selector activity, actual hip-roll motion, lateral velocity, bilateral loads and release timing. Determine whether weaker-side flight and load-bearing advancement improve without sacrificing the stronger side or merely reversing the bias. Record every flight's duration, clearance, advancement, landing load acceptance and delay to opposite-foot release. Report within-segment alternating runs, landing gaps, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Inspect seed272 before deceleration; evaluate stopping and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r310 produced bilateral qualified landings in all three trials, but all eventually fell backward. Seed273 had already reversed velocity by 5 seconds with both ankle targets at −1. Stronger lateral transfer did not preserve sagittal balance.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce bilateral ankle command-gain magnitude from 2.30 to 2.25, retaining every other r310 coefficient, including hip-roll gain 0.36 and speed-gate compensation. This raises ankle targets by 0.025 throughout command 0.50. Test whether relieving negative ankle demand preserves the observed exchanges while delaying deceleration and backward pitch growth. Reduced progression, lost initiation and forward instability are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r310. Align unclipped ankle targets, negative saturation duration, actual ankle motion, pitch rate, forward velocity and foot placement before deceleration. Determine whether improved balance accompanies advancing load-bearing landings and subsequent opposite-foot release, rather than slower shuffling. Record all flight durations, clearances, advancements, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, height, roll, heading and drift. Evaluate stopping convergence and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r311 restored seed272 survival but lost seed271 initiation and failed seed273 restart. Seed273's reported alternating run crosses the stop and must be split. Uniform ankle relief did not resolve the startup-versus-moving-state tradeoff.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce bilateral ankle speed-gate output magnitude to 1.027464, retaining every other r311 coefficient. At command 0.50 and zero velocity, this approximately restores r310 ankle demand while retaining most of r311's relief during forward motion. Test whether startup compensation, rather than moving-state relief, caused the lost initiation. Increased negative saturation and renewed backward instability are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r311 and r310. Decompose command and speed-gate ankle contributions during the first two seconds of each start, then before deceleration. Align unclipped targets, clipping, actual ankle motion, pitch, velocity, foot placement and bilateral loads. Require advancing landings that accept load and enable opposite-foot release. Record all flight durations, clearances, advancements, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, height, roll, heading and drift. Evaluate stopping and restart separately; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r312 did not recover seed271 initiation; all three trials fell. Seed272's touchdown at 13.06 occurred after its upright prefix and must be excluded. Seed273 accumulated substantial heading and lateral drift before restart. Matching zero-velocity ankle demand alone was insufficient.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce selector-driven hip-roll magnitude from 0.36 to 0.35 while retaining every other r312 coefficient. The earlier increase at r310 improved some bilateral contacts but lost survival. Test whether less aggressive lateral transfer improves support continuity and initiation with the current ankle-demand profile. Insufficient unloading and renewed unilateral stepping are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r312. Align selector contributions, hip-roll motion, lateral velocity, bilateral loads and releases, especially seed271's first two commanded seconds. Determine whether reduced lateral excursion permits advancing landings with load acceptance and subsequent opposite-foot release. Measure every flight's duration, clearance and advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Assess stopping convergence and restart separately, including residual stance asymmetry. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r313 survived all three profiles, but walking remained near 0.20 m/s with predominantly left qualified landings. Seed272's 15.02-second landing is post-stop; seed273's cross-stop transition must also be excluded. Survival improved without sustained reciprocal stepping.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce selector foot-separation sensitivity from magnitude 4.50 to 4.25, retaining every other r313 coefficient. Test whether weaker placement-driven selector reversal gives advancing swings more time to complete before support changes. This changes coordination across hips, knees and ankles, not just swing excursion. Delayed support exchange, overreach and renewed falls are risks. Matched hidden pairs preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r313. Decompose selector inputs and align reversals with bilateral foot separation, release, hip/knee motion, recontact and load acceptance. Test whether weaker-side flights become useful advancing landings followed by opposite-foot release, rather than merely longer flights or reversed side bias. Record every flight's duration, clearance and advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Assess standing, stopping convergence and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r314 improved seed271's bilateral qualifications but reversed the dominant side in settled starts and lost survival in seeds271 and273. Seed271 was already moving backward before stopping. Qualified flight durations remained 0.08 seconds, so longer useful swing is not established.

plan.hypothesis: Increase selector foot-separation sensitivity from 4.25 to 4.375, retaining every other r314 coefficient. Test whether partial restoration limits over-advancement and restores support timing while retaining bilateral landings. The endpoint results suggest sensitivity, not guaranteed midpoint stability. Renewed unilateral stepping or early reversal are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r314 and r313. Align placement-driven selector contributions and reversals with release, foot advancement, actual hip/knee motion and landing loads. Inspect seed273 before its four-second divergence and seed271 before deceleration. Require advancing landings that accept load and enable opposite-foot release. Record qualified and unqualified flight durations, clearance, advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Evaluate stopping convergence and restart separately; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r315 preserved settled-start survival and improved seed272 alternation, but seed271 remained left-only. Seed273 produced no qualified landings and fell forward before stopping. Foot-separation retuning alone has not produced robust support replacement.

plan.hypothesis: Increase selector-driven hip-pitch contrast from 0.190 to 0.195 while preserving its coefficient sum at 0.080. Retain every other r315 coefficient, including foot-separation sensitivity 4.375. Test whether slightly stronger reciprocal hip motion restores useful advancement during direct initiation without disturbing the improved seed272 exchanges. Earlier benefits at this contrast were configuration-dependent; overreach, braking and backward instability remain risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r315. Align differential hip targets, actual hip motion, selector reversals, bilateral foot advancement, release and landing loads. Inspect seed273 before five seconds: distinguish insufficient advancement from short flight or failed load acceptance. Require advancing landings followed by opposite-foot release. Record every flight's duration, clearance and advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Evaluate standing, stopping and restart separately; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r316 restored seed273's initial walking but not restart survival, while seed272 lost survival and alternation. Seed271 remained left-only. Stronger hip excursion did not establish reliable reciprocal support; brief releases remain common.

plan.hypothesis: Increase selector-driven knee contrast from 0.564 to 0.574 while preserving its coefficient sum at 0.219. Retain every other r316 coefficient. Test whether stronger differentiation between swing shortening and stance extension improves clearance and support replacement without increasing common selector-driven knee demand. Excessive extension, landing impacts and mistimed flexion are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r316. Separate common and differential knee contributions; align actual knee motion, pelvis height, bilateral loads, foot release, clearance and recontact with selector activity. Determine whether previously brief releases become advancing load-bearing landings followed by opposite-foot release. Record every flight's duration, clearance and advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Inspect seed272 before deceleration and seed273's first two restart seconds. Evaluate standing and stopping separately; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r317 restored seed272 survival and seed273 restart, but seed271 physically collapsed despite horizon termination. Its 15.26-second touchdown is a collapse contact. Seed273's reported five-landing alternating run crosses the stop; its restart run is R-L-R. Sustained walking remains substantially below 0.50 m/s.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce the knee-selector coefficient sum from 0.219 to 0.214 while preserving contrast 0.574. Retain every other r317 coefficient. Test whether slightly less common knee flexion improves support height and load acceptance while retaining the stronger reciprocal knee action. Reduced clearance, harder impacts and disrupted unloading are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r317. Separate common and differential knee targets; align actual knee angles, pelvis height and vertical velocity, bilateral loads, clearance and landing timing. Determine whether improved support permits advancing landings followed by opposite-foot release without shortening useful swings. Inspect seed271 before forward acceleration and seed273 restart. Record every flight's duration, clearance and advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Evaluate standing and stopping separately. Treat physical collapse as failure regardless of termination label; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r318 restored seed271 survival and retained seed272 survival, with bilateral qualified landings in both. However, seed273 lost restart survival despite reaching a near-stationary upright stance. The knee common-demand change traded robustness across profiles rather than uniformly improving support.

plan.hypothesis: Increase the knee-selector coefficient sum from 0.214 to 0.2165 while preserving contrast 0.574. Retain every other r318 coefficient. Test whether partial restoration provides enough knee compliance for restart without sacrificing settled-start support. Endpoint results do not guarantee a stable midpoint; renewed forward collapse or insufficient clearance remain risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r318 and r317. Align common knee targets, actual knee motion, pelvis height and vertical velocity, landing loads and subsequent opposite-foot release. Inspect seed273's first two restart seconds, including its initial stance and lateral velocity; distinguish failed unloading from failed load acceptance. Record all flight durations, clearances and advancements, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Assess standing and stopping separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation; physical collapse is failure regardless of termination label.

proposal.diagnosis: r319 survived all three profiles, including restart, but qualified landings remained sparse and often repeated on one side. Walking stayed near 0.20 m/s rather than 0.50 m/s. Improved survival has not established sustained reciprocal support exchange.

plan.hypothesis: Increase own-foot contact-gated hip-flexion magnitude from 0.0075 to 0.010, retaining every other r319 coefficient. At command 0.50, the additional negative hip target is approximately 0.00241 when airborne versus 0.000088 when planted. Test whether selectively advancing released feet improves useful swing completion without increasing selector-driven hip excursion throughout stance. Overreach, braking and disrupted landing acceptance are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r319. Separate contact-gated and selector-driven hip contributions; align actual hip motion, release, foot advancement, clearance, recontact and landing loads. Determine whether weaker-side releases become advancing landings followed by opposite-foot release, without sacrificing the stronger side. Record all flights, including unqualified releases, and calculate alternating runs and landing gaps separately within each walking segment. Report upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, clipping, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Assess standing, stopping convergence and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration, post-stop qualifications and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r320 retained seed271 survival but reduced its alternation; seed272 fell backward and seed273 failed restart. Stronger airborne hip flexion did not reliably improve useful stepping. Walking remained near 0.20 m/s, far below the target.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce own-foot contact-gated hip-flexion magnitude from 0.010 to 0.00875, retaining every other r320 coefficient. Test whether partial reduction preserves advancing swings while improving landing acceptance and restart. The stable r319 endpoint does not guarantee midpoint stability. Insufficient advancement and continued backward collapse remain risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched profiles with r320 and r319. Align contact-gated hip targets, actual hip motion, foot placement relative to pelvis, landing loads, velocity changes and subsequent opposite-foot release. Inspect seed272 before deceleration and seed273's first two restart seconds. Record qualified and unqualified flights, clearance, advancement, within-segment alternating runs and landing gaps. plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r399. Align contact-gated hip targets and actual motion with touchdown position relative to pelvis, landing loads and velocity loss. proposal.diagnosis: r400 restored seed272's full-trial survival with six alternations, but stepping remained right-biased and slow. Seed271 still failed to initiate sustained release; seed273 stopped upright but failed on restart. Increasing airborne hip extension has not resolved these initiation failures.

plan.hypothesis: Increase bilateral hip-roll selector magnitude from 0.385 to 0.405, retaining every other r400 coefficient. Earlier lateral-gain changes restored some releases, but excessive sway, premature unloading and disrupted landings remain risks. Paired terms preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r400. Align selector differences, hip-roll targets and actual motion with lateral pelvis velocity, bilateral loads, release and landing acceptance. Seed271 still remained planted. Stronger lateral actuation improved one trajectory without robust initiation or landing stability.

plan.hypothesis: Set bilateral hip-roll selector magnitude to 0.395, retaining every other r401 coefficient. plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r401 and r400. plan.hypothesis: Reduce selector foot-x separation sensitivity from magnitude 4.125 to 3.875, retaining every other r402 coefficient. plan.hypothesis: Reduce bilateral hip-pitch angular-rate feedback from 0.145 to 0.135, retaining every other r415 coefficient. proposal.diagnosis: r426 recovered seed273's initial walking and stop, but restart still caused backward collapse. Seeds271/272 remained dominated by repeated same-side landings and fell; seed272 was already unstable before stopping. Knee-contrast tuning has not produced sustained bilateral transfer.

plan.hypothesis: Increase bilateral selector-driven hip-roll gain from 0.395 to 0.405, retaining every other r426 coefficient. Test whether stronger lateral transfer converts existing knee flexion into complete opposite-foot unloading and advancement. Excessive sway, premature transfer and disrupted landing acceptance are risks. Paired terms preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r426. Align selector-driven hip-roll targets and actual motion with pelvis lateral velocity, bilateral loads, knee flexion and opposite-foot release delays. Distinguish insufficient unloading from release followed by premature recontact. Inspect seed271 after its first left landing, seed272 after its switch to repeated left landings, and seed273's launch versus restart. Record all flight durations, clearance, advancement, load-bearing touchdown placement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Evaluate standing, stopping and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation; increased sway or delayed collapse alone is insufficient.

proposal.diagnosis: r427 changed the dominant stepping side without sustaining alternation. Seed273 lost its recovered launch and again recontacted after 0.02 s before planted-foot collapse. Seed272 survived longer but slowed before stopping and subsequently fell backward.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce selector-driven hip-roll gain from 0.405 to 0.400, retaining every other r427 coefficient. Test whether intermediate lateral actuation preserves unloading without prematurely ending swing or disrupting landing acceptance. Outcomes need not interpolate; support locking, unilateral stepping and excessive sway remain risks. Paired terms preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r427 and r426. Prioritize seed273's 0.5–1.2 s interval: align actual hip-roll motion, lateral velocity, bilateral loads, knee flexion and recontact timing. Determine whether restored release leads to advancing load-bearing landings and opposite-foot release. For seeds271/272, measure repeated-side runs and the onset of velocity loss. Record flight durations, clearance, advancement, touchdown placement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, pitch, roll, heading and drift. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation; survival alone is insufficient.

proposal.diagnosis: r428 retained seed273's brief release followed by planted-foot collapse. Seeds271/272 fell backward despite qualified landings; seed272's late alternating burst does not establish stable walking. Hip-roll amplitude interpolation has not resolved transfer timing.

plan.hypothesis: Increase selector roll-rate sensitivity from magnitude 0.06 to 0.07, retaining every other r428 coefficient. Test whether stronger rotational-motion feedback changes selector timing enough to sustain initial unloading and complete support exchanges without increasing hip-roll actuation amplitude. Premature reversal, contact chatter and lost initiation are risks. Matched hidden pairs preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r428. Decompose selector inputs and align roll-rate contributions and reversals with actual hip/knee motion, bilateral loads, release and recontact. Prioritize seed273 from 0.5–1.2 s and seed272 before its late alternating burst; determine whether exchanges preserve forward velocity rather than accompany deterioration. Record all flight durations, clearance, advancement, load-bearing touchdown placement, opposite-foot release delays, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, pitch, roll and heading. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r429 eliminated seed273's brief initial right release without preventing its forward collapse. Seeds271/272 still developed backward falls after sparse exchanges. Increased selector roll-rate sensitivity did not establish sustained alternation.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce selector roll-rate sensitivity from magnitude 0.07 to 0.05, retaining every other r429 coefficient. Test whether weaker rotational feedback allows unloading to develop before selector reversal, rather than suppressing release. This probes below r428's 0.06 rather than restoring that checkpoint. Excessive sway, delayed reversal and harder landings are risks. Matched hidden pairs preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r429 and r428. Align roll-rate and other selector contributions with selector reversals, bilateral loads, actual hip/knee motion, release and premature recontact. Prioritize seed273's first second and seeds271/272 before forward velocity deteriorates. Measure flight duration, clearance, advancement, landing placement and loads, opposite-foot release delay, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, pitch, roll and heading. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately. Require advancing load-bearing exchanges; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r430 restored seed273's initial advancing exchanges, but backward collapse followed its later landings. Seed272 also fell backward shortly after launch. Release alone is insufficient; excessive landing reach or inadequate landing acceptance remains a plausible bottleneck.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce hip-pitch selector contrast from 0.190 to 0.180 while preserving coefficient sum 0.080 and every other r430 coefficient. Test whether smaller differential hip motion reduces landing reach and forward-velocity loss while retaining the restored release sequence. Insufficient advancement and support locking are risks. Paired terms preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r430. Align hip-selector contributions and actual hip motion with touchdown placement, landing loads, velocity change and subsequent opposite-foot release. Prioritize seed273's 2.82–3.0 s landings and seed272 immediately after its first right landing. Record all flights, clearance, advancement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, pitch, roll and heading. Assess initial standing, stopping and restart separately. Require sustained advancing load-bearing exchanges; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: Reducing hip-selector contrast did not prevent backward falls and removed seed273's qualified alternation. Forward speed declined while ankle targets repeatedly saturated negative. Landing geometry alone does not explain the failure.

plan.hypothesis: Increase bilateral ankle speed-gate gain from 1.047464 to 1.077464, retaining every other r431 coefficient. Test whether additional positive ankle contribution at low forward speed interrupts slowing and negative saturation sufficiently to permit continued support exchanges. Altered launch balance, forward collapse and support locking are risks. Paired terms preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r431. Decompose ankle targets into speed-gate, velocity and foot-position contributions before clipping; align saturation onset and actual ankle motion with landing loads, forward deceleration and opposite-foot release. Prioritize seed272 after launch and seed273 from 1–3 s. Record flight duration, clearance, advancement, touchdown placement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, height, pitch, roll and heading. Evaluate standing, stopping and restart separately. Require sustained advancing load-bearing exchanges, not merely delayed falling; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r432 improved seed271's qualified alternation but did not prevent backward collapse. Seeds272/273 fell earlier than in r431. Increasing the positive ankle speed-gate contribution did not arrest slowing; negative saturation may be a consequence rather than the initiating cause.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce bilateral ankle speed-gate gain from 1.077464 to 1.017464, retaining every other r432 coefficient. This probes equally below r431's gain rather than restoring it. Test whether less positive low-speed ankle contribution improves initial forward progression and landing recovery. Premature negative saturation, forward collapse and disrupted release remain risks. Paired terms preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r432 and r431. Measure ankle contributions before clipping, actual ankle motion and forward acceleration during launch and immediately around landings. Determine whether velocity loss precedes saturation and whether changed ankle action enables opposite-foot release. Prioritize seed272's first second after command onset and seed273 before 3 s. Record flight duration, clearance, advancement, landing loads and placement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, height, pitch, roll and heading. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation; survival alone is insufficient.

proposal.diagnosis: r433 allowed seed273 to complete its initial walking and stopping segments, including a six-touchdown alternating run, but restart still failed backward. Seeds271/272 also fell backward. The lower ankle gate gain helped direct launch without resolving settled launch or sustained speed.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce speed-gate velocity sensitivity from magnitude 5.6875 to 5.4375, retaining every other r433 coefficient. Test whether slower gate decay as forward speed rises improves continuation after initial landings without changing its value at zero velocity. This changes all existing h8/h9 pathways, not only the ankles. Lost propulsion, altered lateral transfer and forward collapse are risks. Zero-command paired cancellation is preserved.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r433. Track h8-h9 and its ankle, hip-pitch and hip-roll contributions against velocity, saturation, landing loads and subsequent release. Prioritize seed272 after command onset and seed273's direct launch versus restart. Measure all flight durations, clearance, advancement, touchdown placement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, height, pitch, roll and heading. Assess standing and stopping separately. Exclude cross-stop alternation, collapse contacts and falling acceleration; require sustained advancing load-bearing exchanges.

proposal.diagnosis: Slower speed-gate decay did not resolve settled launch and disrupted seed273's previously sustained initial walking segment. Seed271 survived longer but retained sparse, biased exchanges before falling backward. These results do not support extending the gate contribution as speed rises.

plan.hypothesis: Increase speed-gate velocity sensitivity from magnitude 5.4375 to 5.9375, retaining every other r434 coefficient. This probes faster decay than r433 without restoring that checkpoint. Test whether withdrawing the shared gate contribution earlier preserves forward progression after landing. Zero-velocity gate values and zero-command cancellation remain unchanged. Premature saturation, disrupted lateral transfer and forward collapse are risks.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r434 and r433. Align h8-h9 and all downstream contributions with velocity, actual ankle motion, landing loads, saturation onset and opposite-foot release. Prioritize seed272 immediately after launch and seed273 from 0.8–3 s, then compare direct launch with restart if reached. Record flight duration, clearance, advancement, touchdown placement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, height, pitch, roll and heading. Assess standing and stopping separately. Require sustained advancing load-bearing exchanges; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: Faster gate decay did not prevent backward collapse. Seed273 lost nearly all forward velocity between 1.1 and 1.5 s after landing; seed272 still lacked qualified right steps. Smaller hip-selector contrast has not reliably reduced landing reach or preserved progression.

plan.hypothesis: Increase hip-pitch selector contrast from 0.180 to 0.185, preserving coefficient sum 0.080 and every other r435 coefficient. Test whether modestly stronger differential hip motion improves stance-to-swing progression and opposite-foot advancement with the current speed gate. Increased landing reach, braking and premature recontact are risks. Paired terms preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r435. Align selector contributions and actual hip motion with foot placement, landing loads, forward-velocity change and opposite-foot release. Prioritize seed273 from 1–1.5 s and seed272 after its first left landing. Record all flight durations, clearance, advancement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, pitch, roll and heading. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately. Require sustained advancing load-bearing exchanges; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r436 retained early releases but all trials fell backward. Seed272 produced five qualified right landings without a qualified left landing; seed273 reversed velocity shortly after its first exchanges. Increasing hip contrast did not resolve transfer or landing recovery.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce selector fore-aft foot-separation sensitivity from magnitude 3.875 to 3.625, retaining every other r436 coefficient. Test whether weaker placement-dependent selection prevents an advanced foot from prolonging one-sided stepping or disrupting the next transfer. Mistimed reversal, insufficient swing advancement and support locking are risks. Matched hidden pairs preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r436. Decompose selector inputs into foot separation, roll, lateral velocity and roll rate; align their contributions and selector reversals with bilateral loads, actual hip/knee motion, release and recontact. Prioritize seed272's missing left exchanges and seed273 from 0.8–1.5 s. Record flight duration, clearance, advancement, touchdown placement, landing loads, forward-velocity loss, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height and orientation. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation; require sustained advancing load-bearing exchanges.

proposal.diagnosis: r437 did not resolve seed272's launch failure or seed273's rapid post-landing deceleration. Seed273's feet moved increasingly ahead of the pelvis as pitch became negative. Changing differential selection alone has not stabilized sagittal progression; seed271's eventual forward fall also warns against excessive correction.

plan.hypothesis: Increase hip-pitch selector coefficient sum from 0.080 to 0.090 while preserving contrast 0.185 and every other r437 coefficient. Test whether a small command-gated common hip-extension shift reduces forward foot placement and backward pitching without weakening differential swing motion. Forward collapse, insufficient reach and altered loading are risks. Paired terms preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r437. Separate common and differential hip-selector contributions; measure actual hip motion, bilateral foot positions relative to the pelvis, landing loads, pitch evolution and forward-velocity change. Prioritize seed273 from 1–1.5 s and seed272 immediately after launch. Check whether opposite-foot release follows load acceptance and whether seed271 develops earlier forward instability. Record all flights, clearance, advancement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, roll and heading. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r438 increased seed272's exchanges but did not prevent falling. Seed273's rapid alternating burst accompanied increasing landing reach and velocity reversal, not sustained walking. The faster speed-gate decay remains associated with early direct-launch failure across several revisions.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce speed-gate velocity sensitivity from magnitude 5.9375 to 5.6875, retaining every other r438 coefficient, including hip-selector sum 0.090 and foot-separation sensitivity 3.625. Test whether slower withdrawal of the shared gate contribution restores landing recovery with the changed hip posture. This is an individual coefficient reversal, not a checkpoint restoration. Support locking, altered lateral transfer and forward collapse remain risks; zero-command cancellation is preserved.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r438. Track h8-h9 and every downstream contribution alongside actual ankle/hip motion, touchdown placement, loads, pitch and forward-velocity change. Prioritize seed273 from 1–1.5 s: distinguish sustained advancement from rapid landings that precede braking. Check seed272's opposite-foot release and seed271's late forward instability. Record all flights, clearance, advancement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, slip, saturation, height, roll and heading. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r439 restored longer direct-launch progression, but repeated-side stepping, heading drift and backward instability persisted. Seed273 was already reversing velocity before the stop command. Brief flights and premature recontacts remain a possible bottleneck, not a confirmed cause.

plan.hypothesis: Increase bilateral own-foot contact-gated knee gain from 0.1275 to 0.1475, retaining every other r439 coefficient. Test whether additional airborne flexion prolongs clearance sufficiently for advancing landings and subsequent opposite-foot release. This mainly changes airborne rather than planted knee targets and preserves exact zero-command cancellation. Delayed landing, reduced support height and excessive reach are risks.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r439. Align contact-gate contributions, actual knee flexion, clearance, flight duration and recontact with bilateral loads and opposite-foot release. Distinguish longer useful swings from repeated-side hopping or delayed load acceptance. Prioritize seed273's first 3 seconds and seed272 after its first left landing. Record touchdown advancement and placement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, pitch, height, heading, lateral drift, slip and saturation. Evaluate standing, stopping and restart separately; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r440 increased initial left-foot clearance in seeds271/272, but qualified flights remained 0.08 s and all three trials fell earlier than r439. More airborne flexion did not establish sustained support exchange; clearance alone appears insufficient.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce own-foot contact-gated knee gain from 0.1475 to 0.1375, retaining every other r440 coefficient. Test whether an intermediate gain preserves improved clearance while reducing landing disruption and forward-velocity loss. Outcomes need not interpolate between r439 and r440. Premature recontact and continued support locking remain risks. Paired terms preserve zero-command outputs.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r440 and r439. Prioritize seeds271/272 during the first second after command onset and seed273 from 0.7–1.5 s. Measure actual knee flexion, all flight durations, clearance, touchdown placement, landing loads, velocity change and subsequent opposite-foot release. Determine whether clearance gains translate into load-bearing alternating advancement rather than repeated-side steps. Record within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, height, pitch, roll, heading, lateral drift, slip and saturation. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r441's intermediate knee gain did not improve continuation: all trials fell backward. Seed273 reached 0.227 m/s at its 2.34 s left landing but reversed by 3 s. Landing placement and subsequent braking warrant testing separately from clearance.

plan.hypothesis: Increase bilateral own-foot contact-gated hip-pitch gain from 0.010 to 0.025, retaining every other r441 coefficient. Test whether additional airborne hip extension limits forward reach and reduces landing-associated braking while preserving knee clearance. Insufficient advancement, premature contact and disrupted support exchange are risks. Paired terms preserve exact zero-command cancellation.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r441. Align airborne hip-target changes and actual hip motion with touchdown placement, clearance, landing loads, forward-velocity change and opposite-foot release. Prioritize seed273 around 2.24–3.0 s and seeds271/272 immediately after their early right landings. Determine whether reduced reach preserves forward progression rather than merely suppressing steps. Record all flight durations, advancement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, height, pitch, roll, heading, drift, slip and saturation. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r442 substantially extended stepping in seeds271/272, each reaching an alternating run of six, but both still fell. Seed273 instead repeated right-foot steps while the left foot remained behind the pelvis, then fell forward. Longer flights alone did not produce support exchange.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce own-foot contact-gated hip-pitch gain from 0.025 to 0.0175, retaining every other r442 coefficient. Test whether intermediate airborne extension retains the settled-launch improvement while allowing sufficient advancement and release of the trailing foot during direct launch. Backward braking, renewed short flights and unilateral stepping remain risks; improvement need not interpolate. Zero-command paired cancellation is preserved.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r442 and r441. Prioritize seed273 from 0.7–2 s: track actual hip motion, left-foot trailing distance, bilateral loads and whether right landing leads to left release and advancement. For seeds271/272, distinguish sustained alternating load acceptance from isolated qualified landings. Record all flights, clearance, touchdown placement and advancement, landing-associated velocity change, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, height, pitch, roll, heading, drift, slip and saturation. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r443 restored a left landing in seed273 but not continued exchange; forward velocity fell from 0.197 m/s at 1.14 s to 0.078 at 1.5 s. Seed272 again stalled after one qualified landing. Adjusting airborne hip extension alone has not resolved continuation.

plan.hypothesis: Increase knee-selector contrast from 0.644 to 0.664 while preserving coefficient sum 0.209 and every other r443 coefficient. Test whether stronger differential knee action completes unloading before the airborne contact gate activates, enabling the next support exchange. Excessive stance extension, landing impact and vertical oscillation are risks. Paired terms preserve zero-command cancellation.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r443. Separate selector-driven knee action from contact-gated action; align actual knee motion with bilateral loads, release, clearance and touchdown. Prioritize seed273 after its first right landing and seed272's first second after command onset. Determine whether increased contrast produces opposite-foot release and advancing load acceptance without greater braking. Record all flight durations, landing placement and loads, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, height, pitch, roll, heading, drift, slip and saturation. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r444's stronger knee contrast did not establish sustained alternation: seed271's longest run fell to two, seed272 retained one qualified landing, and seed273 produced only left qualified landings before drifting and falling forward. Greater differential knee amplitude alone was insufficient.

plan.hypothesis: Increase selector lateral-velocity sensitivity from magnitude 1.625 to 1.750, retaining every other r444 coefficient. Test whether stronger motion-dependent selection changes transfer timing enough to interrupt repeated-side stepping and complete opposite-foot unloading. Premature reversal, contact chatter and excessive lateral motion are risks. Matched hidden pairs preserve exact zero-command cancellation.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r444. Decompose selector inputs and align lateral-velocity contributions and selector reversals with bilateral loads, actual hip/knee motion, release and recontact. Prioritize seed273 before heading drift grows and seed272 after its initial left landing. Require advancing load-bearing exchanges with preserved forward velocity, not merely more contact edges. Record all flights, clearance, landing placement and loads, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, height, pitch, roll, heading, drift, slip and saturation. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r445 did not sustain exchanges: seed271 produced eight consecutive qualified right landings after its initial left landing, while seeds272/273 fell backward earlier than r444. Stronger lateral-velocity selection changed release timing but did not prevent braking or unilateral stepping.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce selector lateral-velocity sensitivity from magnitude 1.750 to 1.500, retaining every other r445 coefficient. This probes below r444's 1.625 without restoring that checkpoint. Test whether weaker velocity-driven selection allows load transfer to complete before reversal. Delayed reversal, excessive sway and support locking are risks. Matched hidden pairs preserve zero-command cancellation.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r445 and r444. Align lateral-velocity contributions and selector reversals with bilateral loads, actual hip/knee motion, release and premature recontact. Prioritize seed271's repeated-right sequence and seed273's first left landing and subsequent braking. Measure all flights, clearance, advancement, landing placement and loads, opposite-foot release delay, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, height, orientation, drift, slip and saturation. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately. Require sustained advancing load-bearing exchanges; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: Both lateral-velocity probes left repeated-side stepping and backward collapse unresolved. In r446, forward feet and bilateral negative ankle saturation accompanied slowing before collapse. This motivates testing sagittal feedback rather than another selector-timing adjustment.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce ankle foot-position common gain from -10.25 to -10.00 while preserving own-minus-opposite contrast -6.00 and every other r446 coefficient. Test whether weaker common position feedback reduces negative saturation as feet move ahead, allowing landing recovery and further exchanges. This also changes standing feedback; increased drift, weaker balance recovery and forward collapse are risks.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r446. Decompose unclipped ankle targets into common foot-position, differential placement, velocity and hidden contributions. Align saturation onset and actual ankle motion with landing loads, pitch and velocity loss, especially seed272 after 3.68 s and seed273 from 0.8–2 s. Determine whether reduced saturation enables advancing opposite-foot release rather than simply delaying collapse. Record flight duration, clearance, landing placement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, height, orientation, drift and slip. Explicitly check standing convergence and stopping because zero-command outputs change. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r447 preserved the three-second standing prefixes but reduced every trial to one qualified landing and no alternation. Weaker common ankle position feedback did not prevent negative saturation or backward collapse; saturation may reflect deterioration rather than initiate it.

plan.hypothesis: Increase ankle foot-position common gain from -10.00 to -10.50, preserving own-minus-opposite contrast -6.00 and every other r447 coefficient. This probes equally beyond r446's -10.25 in the opposite direction. Test whether stronger early position feedback maintains pelvis progression relative to the feet before persistent saturation develops. Standing oscillation, harder landing corrections and forward collapse are risks.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r447 and r446. Separate early unsaturated ankle response from later clipping; align actual ankle motion, pelvis-to-foot geometry, landing loads, pitch and forward acceleration. Prioritize the first second after command onset and seed273 from 0.8–1.5 s. Determine whether improved progression enables opposite-foot advancement, rather than simply changing fall direction. Record flight duration, clearance, landing placement, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, height, orientation, drift, slip and saturation. Explicitly assess standing convergence, stopping and restart because zero-command feedback changes. Exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: Neither direction of common ankle position-gain adjustment sustained walking. r448 retained upright standing prefixes but all trials fell backward; seed273 slowed from 0.220 m/s at 1.12 s to 0.031 at 1.5 s. Test command-dependent ankle drive separately from position feedback.

plan.hypothesis: Change bilateral ankle target_vx weights from -2.325 to -2.375, retaining every other r448 coefficient. At command 0.50 this adds -0.025 to each unclipped ankle target. Test whether stronger negative command drive maintains forward progression during launch and landing recovery before persistent saturation. Earlier negative clipping, harder landings and forward collapse are risks. Zero-command outputs remain unchanged.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r448. Track the command contribution, unclipped ankle targets, clipping duration and actual ankle motion against forward acceleration, pitch, foot placement and landing loads. Prioritize seed273 from 0.8–1.5 s and seeds271/272 immediately after their initial landings. Determine whether preserved momentum enables opposite-foot release and advancement rather than falling acceleration. Record all flights, clearance, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, height, orientation, drift and slip. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately; exclude collapse contacts and cross-stop alternation.

proposal.diagnosis: r449 modestly improved seed273's early progression but all three trials still fell backward. Seed273 slowed from 0.216 m/s at 1.12 s to 0.066 at 1.5 s as both feet moved ahead and ankle targets saturated negatively. Stronger command drive did not resolve landing recovery or sustained alternation.

plan.hypothesis: Reduce hip-selector contrast from 0.185 to 0.175 while preserving sum 0.090 and every other r449 coefficient. Test whether smaller differential hip motion reduces excessive landing reach and braking without suppressing opposite-foot advancement. Insufficient reach, support locking and forward collapse are risks. Paired terms preserve exact zero-command cancellation.
plan.readout: Compare matched trials with r449. Align differential hip contributions and actual hip motion with touchdown placement, landing loads, velocity change, pitch and ankle saturation. Prioritize seed273 from 0.8–1.5 s and seeds271/272 after their early right landings. Require advancing load-bearing exchanges, not simply shorter steps or delayed falls. Record all flights, clearance, advancement, opposite-foot release delay, within-segment alternating runs, upright speed error versus 0.50 m/s, height, orientation, drift and slip. Assess standing, stopping and restart separately; exclude collapse contacts, falling acceleration and cross-stop alternation.
